'''Brandon McKinney''' (born August 24, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[San Diego Chargers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2006. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]].  He graduated from [[Chaminade-Julienne High School]].

McKinney has also played for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]].

==Professional career==

===San Diego Chargers===
Brandon McKinney made his NFL debut for the San Diego Chargers in 2006. He was a quality backup nose tackle for two seasons there. McKinney was released by the Chargers on October 4, 2008 following the return of suspended [[linebacker]] [[Stephen Cooper (American football)|Stephen Cooper]].<ref>[http://chargers.com/team/roster/brandon-mckinney.htm Chargers.com - Team » Roster » #91 Brandon McKinney | DT<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070920222255/http://chargers.com/team/roster/brandon-mckinney.htm |date=September 20, 2007 }}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
McKinney was signed by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on October 8, 2008 after [[nose tackle]] [[Kelly Gregg]] was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]]. McKinney, then #68, recovered a fumble from  [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] QB [[Ben Roethlisberger]].

McKinney was re-signed by the Ravens on February 17, 2009, preventing him from becoming a [[restricted free agent]] in the offseason.

In December 2009, the Ravens placed McKinney (now back to #91, which he wore for the San Diego Chargers) on injured reserve due to a back injury after just two tackles in 2009. In 2010, he would come back from injury and record 10 tackles for the Baltimore Ravens.<ref name="bsun_12_20_2009">{{cite news|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bal-sp.ravensscene20dec20,0,3489825.story|title=Bears arrive in Baltimore|last=Hensley|first=Jamison|date=December 20, 2009|work=The Baltimore Sun|accessdate=December 20, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200526085511/https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bal-sp.ravensscene20dec20,0,3489825.story|archive-date=May 26, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
McKinney signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on April 4, 2012.<ref>[http://www.profootballweekly.com/2012/04/04/report-colts-add-dt-mckinney Report: Colts add DT McKinney] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120408035528/http://www.profootballweekly.com/2012/04/04/report-colts-add-dt-mckinney |date=April 8, 2012 }}</ref> On August 6, 2013, McKinney was released with an injury settlement.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/08/06/colts-release-brandon-mckinney-from-ir/ |title=Colts release Brandon McKinney from IR |last=Florio |first=Mike |date=August 6, 2013 |website=NBCSports.com |accessdate=August 7, 2013}}</ref> On June 19, 2014, McKinney was re-signed by the Colts,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.colts.com/2014/06/19/indianapolis-colts-sign-nt-brandon-mckinney |title=Indianapolis Colts sign NT Brandon McKinney |access-date=June 19, 2014 |archive-date=September 3, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903074947/http://blogs.colts.com/2014/06/19/indianapolis-colts-sign-nt-brandon-mckinney/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> but the Colts cut McKinney on August 30, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/colts-insider/2014/08/30/colts-making-final-roster-cuts/14865705/|title=Colts make tough decisions in order to trim roster to 53|access-date=August 30, 2014|archive-date=October 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018073236/http://www.indystar.com/story/colts-insider/2014/08/30/colts-making-final-roster-cuts/14865705/|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Brandon Lamar Jackson''' (born October 2, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the second round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He later won [[Super Bowl XLV]] with the Packers against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]].

==Early life==
Jackson was a two-time Class 5A state [[Offense (sports)|offensive]] player of the year at [[Horn Lake High School]]. He was also named to the Dandy Dozen by the ''[[The Clarion-Ledger|Jackson Clarion-Ledger]]'', signifying the top 12 players in the state of [[Mississippi]].

In 2003, Jackson was a significant driving force taking his team from a 0–5 losing streak to the Mississippi State Playoffs, losing their first round and going out at 5–6.

===Track and field===
Aside from [[High school football|football]] Jackson was also a [[Track and field athletics|track]] star with, he lettered four times in track, and had a career best of 10.6 seconds in the [[100 metres|100 meters]]. He was sixth at state in the 100 as a senior, and helped the 4x200-meter relay squad finish third at state in 2004, while aiding the 4x100 relay squad's fourth-place state finish. He was also part of the 4x400-meter relay team that was second at the Class 5A state meet in 2003.

At the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]], he competed in the [[60 metres|60 meters]] and [[200 metres|200 meters]], recording personal bests of 6.86 seconds and 21.75 seconds, respectively.

==College career==
Jackson played college football at [[Nebraska Cornhuskers|Nebraska]]. During his career at Nebraska he [[Starting lineup|started]] 11 of 33 games, [[Rush (American football)|rushing]] for 1,431 yards on 291 [[Carry (American football)|carries]] and 14 [[touchdown]]s.

===Green Bay Packers===
Jackson was drafted by the Green Bay Packers in the second round of the 2007 NFL Draft with the 63rd overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He scored his first NFL touchdown in [[2007 Green Bay Packers season#Week 3: vs. San Diego Chargers|Week 3]], on September 23, 2007, against the [[San Diego Chargers]]. Jackson topped the 100 yard mark for the first time in his career on December 30, 2007.<ref name="113yards">{{cite web|url=http://www.madison.com/wsj/home/sports//index.php?ntid=264752 |title=Running in relief a thriller for Jackson |publisher=Wisconsin State Journal |access-date=January 1, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090707140025/http://www.madison.com/wsj/home/sports/index.php?ntid=264752 |archive-date=July 7, 2009 }}</ref> On January 2, 2008, Jackson was voted NFL Rookie of the Week for his performance against the [[Detroit Lions]] in which he ran the ball 20 times for 113 yards and made two receptions for 22 yards in the Packers 34–13 victory. In the 11 games he played in, Jackson rushed for 267 yards on 75 carries and a touchdown and added 130 yards on 16 [[Reception (American football)|receptions]].<ref>{{cite web  |last= Packers.com | title = RB Brandon Jackson Voted NFL Rookie Of The Week | url=http://www.packers.com/news/releases/2008/01/02/2/| access-date = January 2, 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080105031913/http://www.packers.com/news/releases/2008/01/02/2/ <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = January 5, 2008}}</ref>

Jackson played in 13 games during his 2008 season, rushing for 248 yards on 45 carries and a touchdown, with 30 receptions for 185 yards. In 2009, Jackson ran for 111 yards in 12 games on 37 attempts, with two rushing touchdowns and a receiving touchdown.

When starter [[Ryan Grant (running back)|Ryan Grant]] suffered ligament damage to his ankle during the first game of the 2010 season, Jackson was named the starter. During the regular season, Jackson achieved new career highs with 703 yards rushing and 342 yards receiving. However, Jackson would later lose his starting job to rookie RB [[James Starks]].

At the end of the 2010 season, Jackson and the Packers appeared in [[Super Bowl XLV]] against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He had one reception for 14 yards in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201102060pit.htm |title=Super Bowl XLV - Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Green Bay Packers - February 6th, 2011 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Jackson was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] on July 29, 2011. He suffered a toe injury in the preseason, and was placed on the injured reserve list in September. On May 16, 2013, he signed a one-year contract to stay with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brandon-jackson-cleveland-browns-strike-contract-0ap1000000201115|title = Brandon Jackson, Cleveland Browns strike contract| website=[[NFL.com]] }}</ref>

==Post-retirement==

'''Brandon Jerome Mebane''' {{Respell|MEE|bayn}};<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Mebane Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MebaBr99.htm |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> (born January 15, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He attended [[Crenshaw High School]] in Los Angeles. He played [[college football]] for the [[California Golden Bears football|California Golden Bears]]. He was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the third round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He also played in the NFL for the [[San Diego Chargers|San Diego]] / [[Los Angeles Chargers]].

==College career==
[[File:BrandonMebane.jpg|thumb|175px|left|Mebane at California]]
Mebane played four seasons at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], recording 109 tackles, 25.5 tackles for a loss, 14.5 sacks, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery for the [[California Golden Bears football|Golden Bears]].

===Seattle Seahawks===
Mebane was selected by the [[2007 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] in the third round, 85th overall of the [[2007 NFL draft]], and on July 24, he signed a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In his rookie season, he played all 16 games and recorded 29 tackles including two sacks. 2008 was a promising year for Mebane as he again played all 16 games and recorded 39 tackles, 5.5 sacks, and 2 forced fumbles. With the departure of [[Rocky Bernard]], Mebane was expected to make a big impact for the Seahawks in 2009 in which he started 15 games and recorded 49 tackles and 1.5 sacks.  For the 2010 season Mebane started the first four games but suffered a calf injury and was forced to sit out the next four games. In the first four games, he had 8 tackles and 1 sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Mebane 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MebaBr99/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Mebane has been a constant in the middle and helped the 2013–2014 [[Legion of Boom (Seattle Seahawks)|Seahawks defense]] reach dominant heights, as they had one of the best seasons in NFL history. The Seahawks eventually won Super Bowl XLVIII against the Denver Broncos, 43–8.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLVIII - Seattle Seahawks vs. Denver Broncos - February 2nd, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201402020den.htm |access-date=November 3, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Mebane, along with defensive linemen [[Red Bryant]], center [[Max Unger]] and punter [[Jon Ryan]], were the only four holdovers on the Super Bowl winning team roster from pre-Carroll/Schneider era.
[[File:Brandon Mebane vs Ravens 2015.jpg|175px|thumb|left|Mebane with the Seahawks in 2015.]]
Fellow Seahawks teammate [[Richard Sherman (American football)|Richard Sherman]] was quoted as saying of Mebane: "He's an incredibly technical player in his movements and everything he does. He's rarely out of position and he's rarely out of the play. You rarely see a defensive tackle running making tackles on the sideline, or [making] tackles on screen plays. He does all that. But once again, he's overlooked because I guess he's not a big sack-total guy. He's just a guy that does his job incredibly well week in and week out."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/seattle-seahawks/post/_/id/9126/sherman-lobbies-for-wagner-and-mebane|title=Richard Sherman lobbies for Bobby Wagner and Brandon Mebane in Pro Bowl|date=October 9, 2014}}</ref>

===San Diego / Los Angeles Chargers===
On March 9, 2016, Mebane signed a three-year contract with the [[San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=March 9, 2016 |title=Bolts Beef Up D-Line with NT Brandon Mebane |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/bolts-beef-up-d-line-with-nt-brandon-mebane-128801 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>

On September 5, 2016, Mebane was named one of the San Diego Chargers team captains for the 2016 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=September 5, 2016 |title=Chargers Announce 2016 Team Captains |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-2016-team-captains-136741 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 14, 2016, with a torn bicep.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=November 14, 2016 |title=Brandon Mebane Out for Season with Biceps Injury |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/brandon-mebane-out-for-season-with-biceps-injury-142221 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>

On March 13, 2019, Mebane re-signed with the Chargers on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=March 13, 2019 |title=Chargers Bring Back NT Brandon Mebane |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-bring-back-nt-brandon-mebane |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>

Mebane was released on March 13, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 13, 2020 |title=Chargers Make Pair of Roster Moves, Part Ways with Thomas Davis Sr. and Brandon Mebane |work=Chargers.com |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-release-thomas-davis-sr-and-brandon-mebane |access-date=March 13, 2020}}</ref>

On November 20, 2020, Mebane announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Sam |date=November 20, 2020 |title=Brandon Mebane Announces Retirement |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2020/11/brandon-mebane-announces-retirement |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref>

'''Brandon Randolph McDonald''' (born August 26, 1985) is a former American [[gridiron football]] [[cornerback]]. He was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fifth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]].

McDonald also played for the [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Detroit Lions]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Calgary Stampeders]], [[Ottawa Redblacks]], and [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]].

==College career==
McDonald played Junior College football at [[Jones County Junior College]] and transferred to the [[University of Memphis]] and started two years there. He lettered for two seasons at JCJC under Coach Parker Dykes. He worked as a receiver during his first season and in the secondary in 2004. He also led JCJC in punt returns during junior college.  He was an education major.

==Professional career==

===Cleveland Browns===
McDonald was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fifth round (140th overall) in the [[2007 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He made his NFL debut versus the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] on September 9. McDonald had superb performances in games against the [[Houston Texans]] in which he had 3 tackles, 4 passes defended, and his 1st career interception, and the [[New York Jets]] in which he had 5 tackles, 2 passes defensed and 1 interception.

He finished the season with 16 games played including 2 starts, 24 tackles, 10 passes defensed, and 2 interceptions.

After an injury to teammate [[Daven Holly]], McDonald started for the Cleveland Browns in 2008. He recorded 64 tackles, 11 assists and 5 interceptions. On December 15, 2008, against the Eagles, McDonald returned an interception, right before halftime, 98 yards only to be tackled out of bounds at the 7 yard line. This play set the record for the longest return in NFL history to not result in a touchdown. Later in the game, McDonald did return an interception 22 yards for a touchdown,

The 2009 campaign for Brandon McDonald was a difficult one for him, after being burned many times and eventually being replaced in the starting lineup by [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] [[Mike Adams (safety)|Mike Adams]] who outperformed him. He recorded 55 tackles, 1 sack, and 1 interceptions in the 2009 season. 2009 was also the year [[Steve McNair]] was murdered. He was Brandon Mcdonald's cousin.

McDonald was cut a week before the start of the 2010 season.

===Arizona Cardinals===
On September 5, 2010, McDonald was claimed off waivers by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] from the Browns. He was waived on October 26.

===Detroit Lions===
On October 27, 2010, McDonald was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Lions]].

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
McDonald was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on August 20, 2012.

===Miami Dolphins===
On November 7, 2012, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Miami Dolphins]].

McDonald was signed by the [[Calgary Stampeders]] on July 16, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stampeders.com/roster/show/id/7055 |title=Brandon McDonald |publisher=stampeders.com |accessdate=29 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810140709/http://www.stampeders.com/roster/show/id/7055 |archivedate=August 10, 2014 }}</ref> He was released by the Stampeders on September 3, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.calgarysun.com/2014/09/04/calgary-stampeders-notebook----jamar-wall-cant-pick-em-all | title=Calgary Stampeders notebook -- Jamar Wall can't pick 'em all | publisher=calgarysun.com | date=September 3, 2014 | accessdate=September 11, 2014 | author=Fisher, Scott | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041350/http://www.calgarysun.com/2014/09/04/calgary-stampeders-notebook----jamar-wall-cant-pick-em-all | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Brandon Anthony Middleton''' (born January 2, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Middleton was signed by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2004. After playing [[college football]] for the [[Houston Cougars football|Houston Cougars]], he played five seasons in the NFL, including the final two with the [[Detroit Lions]]. His top game in "Motown" came on Dec. 16, 2007, at San Diego when Middleton made four grabs for 32 yards and a nine-yard touchdown reception.

==Early life==
Middleton played wide receiver for the Alief Elsik Rams - a suburb of west Houston in Texas - under head coach Bill Barron and wide receiver coach Daniel McKamie during high school. He once had a 101-yard kick off return and was the leading receiver in both catches, yards and TD's. He was also the strongest skills position player on the team at that time and once squatted 415 pounds. Middleton was also a letter man in football and track.

==Professional career==

===Detroit Lions===
Middleton was cut by the Lions on September 12, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=3015884|title=Lions add RB depth with Aveion Cason and cut WR Brandon Middleton|agency=Associated Press|publisher=ESPN|date=September 12, 2007|access-date=July 31, 2024}}</ref> Due to an injury to starting wide receiver [[Roy Williams (wide receiver)|Roy Williams]] late in the 2007 season, Middleton was added from the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3142954|title=Injured Williams hopes to return for season finale at Green Bay|agency=Associated Press|publisher=ESPN|date=December 5, 2007|access-date=July 31, 2024}}</ref> On December 15, 2007 in a game against the [[San Diego Chargers]], Middleton caught his first career touchdown on a pass from quarterback [[Jon Kitna]].

Middleton was released by the Lions during final cuts on August 30, 2008. He was re-signed on September 9 after [[tight end]] [[Dan Campbell]] was placed on [[injured reserve]]. Middleton was released by the Lions on November 11, 2008 and replaced by [[John Standeford]].

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
Middleton was signed to the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] [[practice roster]] on September 16, 2009. He was released on October 4.

==Coaching career==
Middleton was named outside receivers coach for his alma mater [[Houston Cougars]] in February, 2011. Middleton was hired by Houston head coach [[Tony Levine]] after helping Evangel Christian Academy to the Louisiana Class 2A state playoffs in 2011 and the state championship in 2010. During the 2010 championship run, Middleton's top three receivers combined for 148 catches, 2,386 yards and 30 touchdowns as Evangel went 12–2. In 2016 Middleton came to [[Little Rock Christian Academy]] to be offensive coordinator of the Warriors. In the 2018 season, he coached the team to a 9–1 season and the Arkansas 5A state championship.

Middleton was also the offensive coordinator at Royal High School in Brookshire, Texas.

'''Brandon Josiah LaFell'''<ref>{{cite web | title=ESPN Profile | work= ESPN.com | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/12576 }}</ref> (born November 4, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]]. He was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the third round of the [[2010 NFL draft]], and has also played for the [[New England Patriots]], where he was a member of the [[Super Bowl XLIX]] winning team, the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], and the [[Oakland Raiders]].

==Early life==
LaFell attended [[Lamar High School (Houston, Texas)|Lamar High School]] in Houston, where he played football, basketball, and ran track. He was coached by Tom Nolen. In [[high school football|football]], LaFell caught 46 passes for 1,116 yards and 16 touchdowns as a senior. Also starring on special teams, he returned punts of 65 and 58 yards for touchdowns. LaFell was a member of the Houston Chronicle Top 100 and named first-team All-Greater Houston Area in 2004. In [[basketball]], LaFell was a standout [[point guard]]. In [[track and field]], LaFell competed in the [[high jump]] event.

==College career==
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his initial year at LSU, LaFell saw action in 11 of the Tigers’ 13 games in 2006. His first career play was a 58-yard touchdown reception against [[University of Louisiana at Lafayette|Louisiana-Lafayette]] in week one. On the year, LaFell caught five passes that went for 140 yards and two touchdowns. He received Freshman All-SEC honors by the coaches.

In 2007, as a sophomore, LaFell played in all 14 games with nine starts. He ranked first on team in receiving yards (656) and second in receptions (50), while catching four touchdown passes and averaging 13.1 yards a reception. LaFell helped LSU to win the [[NCAA Division I FBS National Football Championship|BCS National Championship]] that year.

As a junior, LaFell emerged as one of the top receivers in the country, as he caught 63 passes for 929 yards and eight touchdowns. He ranked second in the SEC in yards per game with 71.5 per contest and was third in the league with 4.8 receptions per contest. LaFell subsequently earned First-team All-SEC honors by the [[Associated Press]].

LaFell was considered one of the best wide receivers in his draft class, and drew comparisons to [[Dwayne Bowe]], another wide receiver out of LSU.<ref>{{Citation |last=Rang |first=Rob |date=July 10, 2009 |title=Top 32 seniors: Top heavy with the heftier prospects |newspaper=NFLDraftScout.com |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/story/11942391 }}</ref><ref name="CBS Sports ranking">{{Citation |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/prospectrankings/TSX/2010_WR |title=2010 NFL Draft WR ranking |work=CBS Sports |access-date=February 8, 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brandt |first=Gil |author-link=Gil Brandt |date=July 23, 2009 |title=Next year's top receiver prospects feature a variety of skills |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story?id=09000d5d810f6578 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On April 23, 2010, LaFell was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the third round, 78th overall.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Despite not starting over [[Steve Smith (American football, born 1979)|Steve Smith]] and [[David Gettis]], he gradually gained playing time, eventually taking the #3 slot at receiver. He recorded his first NFL touchdown in Week 8 against the [[St. Louis Rams]], a 17-yard pass from [[Matt Moore (American football)|Matt Moore]].

He finished the season with 38 catches for 468 yards; his longest catch was of 44 yards. He also gained 60 additional yards on the ground, all of which came on a single [[end-around]] play in Week 17 against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], his longest gain of the season.

LaFell set a [[Carolina Panthers]] franchise record on Christmas Eve in 2011 with a 91-yard touchdown catch from rookie quarterback [[Cam Newton]]. It was the longest pass play in Panther history.

===New England Patriots===
On March 15, 2014, LaFell signed a three-year, $9 million contract with the [[New England Patriots]]. He chose to wear #19 because friend and former teammate [[Ted Ginn Jr.]] wears the same number.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brandon-lafell-to-sign-with-new-england-patriots-0ap2000000334408|title=Brandon LaFell to sign with New England Patriots|first=Gregg|last=Rosenthal|date=March 15, 2014|access-date=March 16, 2014}}</ref> Against the [[Chicago Bears]] in Week 8, LaFell recorded a career-high eleven catches for 124 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-lunchWithLarry/Lunch-with-Larry-102814/edfd4e56-ca9c-4f51-8558-fc5c0e432dd5|title=Lunch with Larry 10.28.14|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=October 28, 2014|access-date=November 22, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141113035312/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-lunchWithLarry/Lunch-with-Larry-102814/edfd4e56-ca9c-4f51-8558-fc5c0e432dd5|archive-date=November 13, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2014, LaFell had his most prolific season, recording 74 catches for 953 yards and 7 touchdowns. LaFell helped the Patriots finish 12–4. In the divisional round against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], with the Patriots down 31–28, LaFell caught the game-winning touchdown to help the Patriots defeat the Ravens 35–31. In [[Super Bowl XLIX]], LaFell had 4 catches for 29 yards and the first touchdown of the game as the Patriots defeated the [[Seattle Seahawks]] 28–24.

LaFell started the 2015 season on [[Physically unable to perform|PUP]] with a foot injury and missed the first five games of the season before returning in New England's 30–23 win over the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-wideout-brandon-lafell-headed-to-pup-list-0ap3000000523227 |title=Patriots wideout Brandon LaFell headed to PUP list |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=September 5, 2015 |website=NFL.com |access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-activate-wr-brandon-lafell-from-pup-0ap3000000564277 |title=Patriots activate WR Brandon LaFell from PUP |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=October 24, 2015 |website=NFL.com |access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref> LaFell struggled throughout the 2015 season with multiple drops and failed to live up to his career performance the previous year.

On March 2, 2016, LaFell was released by the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-release-brandon-lafell-scott-chandler-0ap3000000640824 |title=Patriots release Brandon LaFell, Scott Chandler |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=March 2, 2016 |website=NFL.com |access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots release TE Scott Chandler and WR Brandon LaFell|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2016/03/02/patriots-release-te-scott-chandler-and-wr-brandon-lafell|website=Patriots.com|date=March 2, 2016|access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===

On March 30, 2016, LaFell signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000648994/article/cincinnati-bengals-agree-to-deal-with-brandon-lafell|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330234706/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000648994/article/cincinnati-bengals-agree-to-deal-with-brandon-lafell|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 30, 2016|title=Cincinnati Bengals agree to deal with Brandon LaFell|first=Kevin|last=Patra|date=March 30, 2016|access-date=March 30, 2016}}</ref>

On September 11, 2016, LaFell made his Bengals debut in a 23–22 victory over the [[2016 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. He had four receptions for 91 yards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110nyj.htm|title=Cincinnati Bengals at New York Jets - September 11th, 2016|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=November 27, 2017}}</ref> He played 16 games in [[2016 Cincinnati Bengals season|2016]], starting 14 of them as the Bengals went 6–9–1 and missed the playoffs. He finished the season with 64 receptions for 862 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LaFeBr00.htm|title=Brandon LaFell|work=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=November 27, 2017}}</ref>

On March 8, 2017, LaFell signed a two-year contract extension with the Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-re-sign-wr-brandon-lafell-0ap3000000791533 |title=Bengals re-signing WR Brandon LaFell |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=March 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com |access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>

On September 10, 2017, LaFell began the [[2017 Cincinnati Bengals season|2017 season]] with three receptions for 24 yards in a 20–0 loss to the [[2017 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100cin.htm|title=Baltimore Ravens at Cincinnati Bengals - September 10th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=September 24, 2017}}</ref> He finished the season with 52 receptions for 548 yards and three touchdowns.

On August 2, 2018, Lafell was released by the Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-release-veteran-receiver-brandon-lafell-0ap3000000944048 |title=Bengals release veteran receiver Brandon LaFell |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=August 2, 2018 |website=NFL.com |access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
On September 3, 2018, LaFell signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-sign-receiver-brandon-lafell-to-one-year-deal-0ap3000000957775|title=Raiders sign receiver Brandon LaFell to one-year deal|first=Nick|last=Shook|date=September 3, 2018|access-date=September 3, 2018}}</ref> He played in six games, recording 12 catches for 135 yards and two touchdowns, before suffering a torn Achilles in Week 11.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon LaFell 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LaFeBr00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2024-10-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 19, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2018 |title=Raiders sign wide receiver Keon Hatcher, place LaFell on IR |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-wide-receiver-keon-hatcher-place-lafell-on-ir |access-date=2024-10-17 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

'''Brandon Latrel Keith''' (born November 21, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Northern Iowa Panthers football|Northern Iowa Panthers]]. Keith was selected by the Cardinals in the seventh round of the [[2008 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Keith attended [[McAlester High School]] in [[McAlester, Oklahoma]], where tallied over 70 pancake blocks earned first-team all-state honors from the ''[[Daily Oklahoman]]'' and the ''[[Tulsa World]]'' as a senior in 2002.

Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Keith was rated as the No. 20 offensive tackle in the nation.<ref>{{Citation |date=January 30, 2003 |title=Rivals.com Offensive tackles 2003 |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=187 }}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Oklahoma]], but did not qualify academically, and eventually headed for [[junior college]].

==College career==
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his first year at [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College]], Keith received first-team all-Southwest League honors and second-team NJCAA All-American in 2004. Honoring his commitment to the Sooners, Keith was a member of the [[2005 Oklahoma Sooners football team]] but did not see action. Unsatisfied with his role, he decided to transfer to the [[University of Northern Iowa]].

Keith saw action in seven games for the [[Northern Iowa Panthers football|Panthers]], and started two. He missed four games with a bone bruise in his right knee. Keith was part of the offense ranked No. 11 in the nation in scoring (31.0 points/game) in 2006.

In 2007, Keith started 11 games at right tackle, helping to guide the Panthers to a perfect 11–0 regular season and a No. 1 national ranking for six weeks. He received ''[[Associated Press]]'' All-America third-team honors and was named an honorable mention All-American by ''The Sports Network''.

==Professional career==
Despite impressive showings at Northern Iowa's Pro Day, where he ran a sub-5.0 [[40-yard dash]] at 345 pounds, Keith was not regarded as one of the top offensive tackles in the draft, due to his unpolished footwork and lack of consistency.<ref name="TSN war room">{{Citation |work=SportingNews.com |date=April 28, 2008 |title=Pro Football War Room: Brandon Keith |url=http://warroom.sportingnews.com/nfl/draft/2008/players/8169.html }}</ref> He was selected in the seventh round with the 225th overall pick by the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Brandon Gerrod Miller''' (born January 21, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2008. He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]].

He also played for the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

== Early life ==
Attended  Miller County High School and as a senior he made 106 tackles and 27 receptions for more than 500 yards. He was named All-State, and All-South and  was  named SuperPrep Elite 50, All-America, and All-Dixie Teams.

== College career ==
Miller played in 37 career games with 15 starts at linebacker for Georgia, posting 73 tackles and 6.0 sacks in his Bulldog career. In 2007, he appeared in 11 games making seven starts and in 2006 he appeared in every game with five starts and made 23 tackles with 2 PBU and 3 QB-Pressures. In 2005, he made his first career start against Boise State in the 2005 opener and started 10 games during season despite being hampered by injuries The prior season, 2004, he played in all 12 games with nine tackles and one fumble recovery.

== Professional career ==

===Atlanta Falcons===
He was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2008. He spent the first 10 weeks of the regular season on the team's [[practice squad]] before being promoted to the active roster on November 16. He was waived two days later.

===Seattle Seahawks===
Miller was claimed off waivers by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on November 19, 2008. He appeared in one game for the Seahawks during the 2008 season, recording one tackle.

Miller was waived/injured by the Seahawks on July 29 and subsequently reverted to the team's [[injured reserve]] list.  On May 13, 2010, Miller was released by the Seahawks.

'''Brandon Montez Lang''' (born June 18, 1986 in [[Tucker, Georgia]]) is a [[gridiron football]] [[defensive end]]. He attended [[Troy University]], where he graduated from in 2010. After going undrafted in the [[2010 NFL draft]], he signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the [[San Diego Chargers]].,<ref>{{cite news|title=Chargers release WR Buster Davis as camp opens; Turner impressed with rookie QB Tolzien|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/chargers-release-wr-buster-davis-as-camp-opens-turner-impressed-with-rookie-qb-tolzien/2011/07/28/gIQAFF25fI_story.html|agency=[[Associated Press]]|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|accessdate=29 July 2011}}{{dead link|date=July 2020|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and then was signed by the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] on September 25, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.esks.com/article/eskimos-bulk-up-on-defensive-line |title=Eskimos bulk up on defensive line | Edmonton Eskimos |access-date=2012-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121127042158/http://esks.com/article/eskimos-bulk-up-on-defensive-line |archive-date=2012-11-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was also a member of the [[Orlando Predators]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Orlando Predators Add Former NFL Linebacker Brandon Lang |url=http://www.orlandopredators.com/news/orlando-predators-add-former-nfl-linebacker-brandon-lang-200.php |publisher=[[Orlando Predators]] official website |accessdate=20 January 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120509233242/http://www.orlandopredators.com/news/orlando-predators-add-former-nfl-linebacker-brandon-lang-200.php |archivedate=9 May 2012 }}</ref>

==High school career==
Lang attended [[Tucker High School]] in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], where he helped his team to a 34-4 record over three seasons while playing both tight end and defensive end. Lang was twice named both first-team All-State (AJC) and All-Region. As a defensive player, he recorded 290 career tackles including 71 sacks. He was also credited with 18 career fumble recoveries and 122 tackles for loss.

He initially committed to play football at [[University of Georgia|Georgia]], but instead attended [[Hargrave Military Academy]]. Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Lang was ranked 10th among prep school prospects in 2005.<ref>{{Citation |date=November 2, 2004 |title=Rivals.com Prep School Top 25 2005 |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1056 }}</ref> It has been reported by NFL blogger Gil Brant that Lang signed with the San Diego Chargers as an undrafted free agent shortly after the draft.<ref>{{Citation |date=April 25, 2010 |title=nfl.com Teams begin scramble to sign undrafted players |url=http://www.nfl.com/draft/story?id=09000d5d817c634a&template=with-video-with-comments&confirm=true |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100426161551/http://www.nfl.com/draft/story?id=09000d5d817c634a&template=with-video-with-comments&confirm=true |archivedate=2010-04-26 }}</ref>

==College career==
In 2006, he committed to Troy and became part of the defensive line rotation as a freshman. In 2007, Lang started three games before a knee injury ended his season. In 2008, Lang was rated as the [[Sun Belt Conference]]'s top [[NFL draft]] prospect by [[Sporting News]].<ref>{{Citation|publisher=dothaneagle.com |date=June 16, 2008 |title=Q&A with Troy defensive end Brandon Lang |url=http://www.dothaneagle.com/dea/sports/college/troy/article/qa_with_troy_defensive_end_brandon_lang/27643/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120728225019/http://www.dothaneagle.com/dea/sports/college/troy/article/qa_with_troy_defensive_end_brandon_lang/27643/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 28, 2012 }}</ref>

During the 2008 season, Lang earned 9 sacks and 56 tackles over the 13 game season. Following the year, he was named to the top 100 returning players in college football, ranking at  number 84.<ref>{{Citation |publisher=College Football News |date=January 16, 2009 |title=100 Best Returning Players Of 2009 |url=http://cfn.scout.com/2/830681.html |access-date=January 16, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090118221146/http://cfn.scout.com/2/830681.html |archive-date=January 18, 2009 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===San Diego Chargers===
Shortly after going undrafted in [[2010 NFL draft|2010]], Lang signed with the [[San Diego Chargers]] as a [[free agent]].  He was released by the Chargers on November 22, 2010, but later re-signed. He was released again on July 28, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Chargers release WR Buster Davis as camp opens; Turner impressed with rookie QB Tolzien|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/chargers-release-wr-buster-davis-as-camp-opens-turner-impressed-with-rookie-qb-tolzien/2011/07/28/gIQAFF25fI_story.html|agency=[[Associated Press]]|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|accessdate=29 July 2011}}{{dead link|date=July 2020|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

===Orlando Predators===
Lang was signed by the [[Arena Football League]] team, the [[Orlando Predators]] on December 6, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Preds add former NFL linebacker Brandon Lang|url=http://www.orlandopost.com/uncategorized/preds-add-former-nfl-linebacker-brandon-lang/|publisher=Orlando Post|accessdate=20 January 2013}}</ref>

===Edmonton Eskimos===
Lang was signed by the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] on September 25, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.esks.com/article/eskimos-bulk-up-on-defensive-line |title=Eskimos bulk up on defensive line | Edmonton Eskimos |access-date=2012-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121127042158/http://esks.com/article/eskimos-bulk-up-on-defensive-line |archive-date=2012-11-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
Lang was signed by the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] on February 13, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/article/redblacks-ink-smith-land-three-others |title=FA14: RedBlacks ink Smith, Lang, three others |access-date=2017-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923225152/http://www.cfl.ca/article/redblacks-ink-smith-land-three-others |archive-date=2015-09-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Lang was released by the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] on October 14, 2014.<ref>[http://us9.campaign-archive2.com/?u=d4de6a98c3a55f12911ee7070&id=af98813e59 FA14: News Release: Transactions; October 14, 2014]</ref>

'''Brandon Keith James''' (born December 21, 1987) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[kick returner]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and winning two [[BCS National Championship]]s with the Gators.  Thereafter, he played professionally for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the NFL and the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] of the CFL.

==Early life==
James was born in [[St. Augustine, Florida]] in 1987.<ref name="pfrprofile">{{Cite web |title=Brandon James Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JameBr00.htm |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He attended [[St. Augustine High School (St. Augustine, Florida)|St. Augustine High School]], where he was a standout [[running back]] for the St. Augustine Yellow Jackets [[high school football|high school football team]].<ref name=ufprofile>GatorZone.com, Football History, 2009 Roster, [http://www.gatorzone.com/football/bios.php?year=2008&player_id=47  Brandon James] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151122005122/http://www.gatorzone.com/football/bios.php?year=2008&player_id=47 |date=November 22, 2015 }}. Retrieved August 25, 2010.</ref> As a senior team captain in 2005, James ran for 900 yards and eight [[touchdown]]s while leading the Yellow Jackets to a Florida Class 3A state championship.<ref name=ufprofile/>

==College career==
James received an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida,<ref name=ufprofile/> where he played for coach [[Urban Meyer]]'s [[Florida Gators football]] team from [[2006 Florida Gators football team|2006]] to [[2009 Florida Gators football team|2009]].<ref name=ufmediaguide>''[http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf  2011 Florida Gators Football Media Guide] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402035222/http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf |date=April 2, 2012 }}'', University Athletic Association, Gainesville, Florida, pp. 85, 89, 95, 97, 98, 102, 125, 139, 147–150, 158, 182 (2011).  Retrieved August 30, 2011.</ref>  As a freshman in 2006, James saw immediate playing time as a kick return specialist, returning 33 punts for 363 yards and one touchdown in 2006, and earning Freshman All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) and Freshman All-American honors.<ref name=ufprofile/>  His 33-yard kickoff return against the [[2006 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State Buckeyes]] in the [[2007 BCS National Championship Game]] gave the Gators the ball in Buckeye territory after Ohio State's [[Ted Ginn Jr.]] opened the game with a kickoff return for a touchdown.<ref name=ufprofile/>  James's dramatic return and the Gators' resulting touchdown changed the early momentum of the game, with the Gators ultimately defeating the top-ranked Buckeyes 41–14 to win the BCS National Championship.<ref name=ufprofile/>

James led the Gators in kickoff and punt return yardage for four consecutive seasons, and finished his college career with 4,770 total yards gained, including 112 kickoff returns for 2,718 yards and a touchdown, 117 punt returns for 1,371 yards and four touchdowns, 379 receiving yards and 302 rushing yards.<ref name=ufmediaguide/>  His career kickoff return yardage and combined kick return yardage remain SEC records.<ref name=ufmediaguide/>  He was a first-team All-American in 2007, a consensus first-team All-American in 2008, a first-team All-SEC selection in 2008, the SEC Special Teams Player of the Year in 2008, and a senior team captain in 2009.<ref name=ufmediaguide/><ref>''2012 NCAA Football Records Book'', [http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2012/Awards.pdf  Award Winners], National Collegiate Athletic Association, Indianapolis, Indiana, pp. 11 & 14 (2012).  Retrieved September 14, 2012.</ref>  During his time as a Gator, the team won two [[SEC Championship Game]]s ([[2006 SEC Championship Game|2006]], [[2008 SEC Championship Game|2008]]) and two [[BCS National Championship Game]]s ([[2007 BCS Championship Game|2007]], [[2009 BCS Championship Game|2009]]).

James graduated from the University of Florida with a bachelor's degree in sociology in 2010.

==Professional career==

The [[Indianapolis Colts]] signed James as an undrafted free agent on April 30, 2010.  On November 10, James was activated from the practice squad to the main roster.  On November 28, 2010, James posted 150 kick return yards and 29 punt return yards.<ref name=nflprofile>National Football League, Current Players, [http://www.nfl.com/players/brandonjames/profile?id=JAM112028  Brandon James].  Retrieved March 28, 2011.</ref>  He was released the following week from the Colts active roster.

In {{CFL Year|2011}}, the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] signed James as a free agent,<ref>The Canadian Press, "[https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/story/?id=368393  Eskimos kick returner James ready for fresh start after NFL]," TSN (June 9, 2011).  Retrieved March 1, 2012.</ref> but he was later released during the regular season, bringing his playing career to an end.<ref>Barney, Justin. June 21, 2012. Retrieved February 4, 2013.</ref>

==Coaching career==

In 2012, James was hired to coach the football team at [[St. Joseph Academy (St. Augustine, Florida)|St. Joseph Academy]] in St. Augustine. He was fired after one season in which the team went 2-8.<ref>Klein, Danny. [http://staugustine.com/sports/2013-01-08/st-joseph-parts-ways-brandon-james-football-coach#.URCFtB1Ijm4 "St. Joseph parts ways with Brandon James as football coach"]. staugustine.com. Hughes was signed off the Giants' [[practice squad]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on November 23, 2010, to fill the slot vacated after [[cornerback]] [[Ellis Hobbs]] was placed on the [[injured reserve]].<ref>[http://phillysportsdaily.com/eagles/2010/11/23/eagles-sign-cornerback-place-hobbs-on-ir/ Eagles sign Cornerback, Place Hobbs on IR, ''Philadelphia Sports Daily'', November 23, 2010.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715074630/http://phillysportsdaily.com/eagles/2010/11/23/eagles-sign-cornerback-place-hobbs-on-ir/ |date=July 15, 2011 }}</ref> He played in one game in [[2010 Philadelphia Eagles season|2010]], the final game of the season as the Eagles rested their starters in preparation for the playoffs.<ref>{{cite news |author=Ford, Bob |title=Bob Ford: For Eagles, resting starters isn't the best way to prepare for playoffs |url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-01-03/sports/26356300_1_eagles-lincoln-financial-field-andy-reid |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926212652/http://articles.philly.com/2011-01-03/sports/26356300_1_eagles-lincoln-financial-field-andy-reid |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 26, 2013 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=January 3, 2011 |accessdate=July 29, 2012}}</ref> In [[2011 Philadelphia Eagles season|2011]], Hughes played in 13 games, started one, and recorded 16 tackles throughout those games.
On September 23, 2012, the Eagles announced that they signed Hughes to a one-year extension. On September 7, 2013, Hughes was released by the Eagles. On September 10, 2013, Hughes was re-signed by the Eagles. On September 23, 2013, Hughes was released by the Eagles with an injury settlement.

===Cleveland Browns===
Hughes signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] on January 2, 2014. Hughes was released from the Browns on May 12, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Browns release Vince Young, four others | website=NBC Sports | date=2014-05-12 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/browns-release-vince-young-four-others | access-date=2025-10-27}}</ref>

==Post-football career==
In 2025, Hughes was hired as [[police officer]] by the [[Falls Township, Bucks County, Pennsylvania|Falls Township]] police department in [[Bucks County, Pennsylvania]]. He also owns a gym in [[Middletown Township, Bucks County, Pennsylvania|Middletown Township]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sofield |first1=Tom |title=Former NFL Player Hired As Falls Twp. Police Officer |url=https://levittownnow.com/2025/07/29/former-nfl-player-hired-as-falls-twp-police-officer/ |access-date=30 July 2025 |work=LevittownNow.com |date=29 July 2025}}</ref>

'''Brandon Hogan''' (born April 1, 1988) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for the [[Carolina Panthers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia Mountaineers]]. He was selected by the Panthers in the fourth round of the [[2011 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Brandon Hogan played football at [[Osbourn High School]], where he began to earn respect on the collegiate recruiting scene. As a junior, Hogan passed for 2,045 yards and 18 touchdown, totaling 3,183 yards and 36 touchdowns on the season. In his senior season, Hogan passed for 2,430 yards and rushed for 1,781 yards with 59 total touchdowns as he led Osbourn to an undefeated AAA Division 6 State Championship. Hogan was named All-Metro by ''[[The Washington Post]]'' and all-state his senior year.

On the recruiting scene, Hogan was offered scholarships by [[West Virginia University]], [[University of Kentucky]], [[Marshall University]], [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]], [[University of Virginia]], and [[Virginia Tech]]. Hogan was projected as a [[cornerback]], rather than a quarterback. After a February 2 visit, Hogan chose to accept the scholarship offer at West Virginia.<ref name="Scout.com: Brandon Hogan Profile">{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/west-virginia/?Notification.Info=The%20legacy%20url%20is%20not%20supported|title=WVU Football, Basketball, & Recruiting|website=247sports.com|access-date=December 6, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman season===
After enrolling at [[West Virginia University]] in 2007, Hogan was projected as a [[defensive back]] on the team's roster.<ref name="Scout.com: Brandon Hogan Profile"/> However, Hogan played slot receiver for his debut season. Hogan grabbed 12 receptions on the season for 67 yards, a 5.6 yard per catch average. Hogan saw action on more than 225 plays during the season, including a season-high 55 plays against [[East Carolina University|ECU]]. In that game, Hogan recorded a season-high six receptions for 44 yards.

===Sophomore season===
Hogan began spring practices in April 2008 with an impressive performance in the team's first scrimmage. In the scrimmage, Hogan totaled a team-best six catches for 67 yards and a score and also rushed for a touchdown as he finished with 82 all-purpose yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?sport=football&story=12566|title=Hogan's Hero|last=Antonik|first=John|date=April 5, 2008|website=MSNsportsNET.com|location=Morgantown, West Virginia|language=en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223050207/http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?sport=football&story=12566|archive-date=February 23, 2012}}</ref> In the Gold & Blue Spring Game on April 19, Hogan led all receivers with 6 receptions for 49 yards. However, as fall practice began Hogan made the transition from receiver to [[cornerback]], the position he was projected to play when he arrived at West Virginia as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?story=13022&cat=exclusives|title=Sunshine Boys|last=Caridi|first=Tony|author-link=Tony Caridi|date=August 12, 2008|website=MSNsportsNET.com|location=Morgantown, West Virginia|language=en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223050239/http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?story=13022&cat=exclusives|archive-date=February 23, 2012}}</ref>

Hogan saw his first career start at cornerback in the 27–3 victory over [[Marshall University|Marshall]], in which he recorded four tackles and recovered a fumble. In the 24–17 victory over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]], Hogan had 5 tackles in his second start at corner. Then in the win over [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]], Hogan had 4 tackles. Hogan followed-up the Syracuse game with 3 tackles in the 34–17 win over [[Auburn Tigers|Auburn]].

In the 35–13 win over [[UConn|Connecticut]], Hogan had 3 tackles, a fumble recovery, and two interceptions for a total of 50 return yards. The interceptions were Hogan's first of his career. In the following 26–23 loss in overtime to [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati]], Hogan was second on the team with 9 tackles and two pass break-ups. In the 13–7 victory in the [[South Florida Bulls|USF]] season finale, Hogan led the team with 9 tackles. However, he missed the [[Belk Bowl|Meineke Car Care Bowl]] victory over [[North Carolina Tar Heels|North Carolina]] due to a personal illness issue. Various players honored Hogan during the game, while the team held up Hogan's #22 jersey before the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wvnstv.com/story.cfm?func%3Dviewstory%26storyid%3D49072 |title=Winning it for Hogan - WVNS-TV - WVNSTV.com |access-date=May 11, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718123036/http://www.wvnstv.com/story.cfm?func=viewstory&storyid=49072 |archive-date=July 18, 2011 }}</ref>

Hogan finished his first season at cornerback as a sophomore with 60 tackles, 3 interceptions, seven pass breakups, two fumble recoveries, and two forced fumbles. Hogan played in 12 games and started 9 on the year; he tied for the team lead in interceptions and sixth on the team in tackles. Hogan earned WVU's Defensive Champion honors four times and the Special Teams Champion honor once.

Hogan was suspended indefinitely from the team on September 12, 2010, following a drunk driving arrest in Morgantown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2010 |title=West Virginia CB Hogan suspended indefinitely |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=5572711 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206224211/https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=5572711 |archive-date=December 6, 2021 |access-date=December 6, 2021 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

'''Brandon Lee Graham''' (born April 3, 1988)<ref name=55BG/> is a former American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2009. Graham was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the first round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] with the 13th overall selection and the first from the [[Big Ten Conference]].

In high school, he was a highly rated [[linebacker]] who served as [[captain (sports)|captain]] for the 2006 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]].  He was listed on numerous All-American lists and was a finalist for some of the highest individual rewards a [[high school football]] player can earn.

Graham was the [[2009 Big Ten Conference football season|2009 Big Ten Conference]] co-[[Most valuable player|MVP]] as recognized by the [[Chicago Tribune Silver Football]] award.  He was the 2009 FBS [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] for a loss (per game) champion after finishing second in 2008 by 0.01 tackles for loss per game.  He was the 2008 and 2009 Big Ten Conference tackles for loss leader. After completing his career as defensive end for the [[2009 Michigan Wolverines football team]], he had a total of 29.5 career [[quarterback sack|sacks]] and 56 career tackles for loss for the [[Michigan Wolverines football]] team.  In 2008, he led the [[Big Ten Conference]] in tackles for loss, with 20 in 11 games.  In 2009, he posted 26 tackles for loss and 10.5 sacks in 12 games.  As a member of the [[2008 Michigan Wolverines football team]] he earned Second-team [[2008 Big Ten Conference football season|2008 Big Ten]] All-conference recognition from both the coaches and the media.<ref name="BTA2FACTAIH">{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2008 |title=Big Ten Announces 2008 Football All-Conference Teams And Individual Honors: Iowa's Green Named Offensive Player of the Year, Ohio State's Laurinaitis repeats as Defensive Player of the Year. |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112408aag.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090918132539/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112408aag.html |archive-date=September 18, 2009 |access-date=October 1, 2009 |website=Big Ten Conference |publisher=CBS Interactive}}</ref> He was a finalist for the [[2009 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2009 NCAA Division I FBS football]] [[Ted Hendricks Award|Hendricks Award]]. He was a First-team 2009 All-Big Ten selection by the coaches and media.<ref name=BTA2FACTaIH9/>  He was named to several First-team and Second-team [[2009 College Football All-America Team|2009 All-America]] lists by various publications. Graham was also named MVP of the [[2010 Senior Bowl]].

Graham was a second team [[2016 All-Pro Team|2016 All-Pro]] selection and a [[2021 Pro Bowl|2020 Pro Bowl]] selection. He led the [[Super Bowl LII]] champion [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in [[quarterback sack]]s with 9.5 during the [[2017 NFL season]]. Graham is responsible for one of the biggest plays in Philadelphia sports history, as he posted a pivotal strip sack on [[Tom Brady]] in the closing minutes of [[Super Bowl LII]], which was the franchise's first Super Bowl victory. He was also a member of the [[2024 Philadelphia Eagles season|2024 team]] which won [[Super Bowl LIX]]. Graham has played more games and more seasons for the Eagles than any other player.<ref name="u934">{{cite web | title=Brandon Graham plays in Philadelphia Eagles record 189th game | website=CBS News | date=2023-11-26 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/philadelphia-eagles-defensive-end-brandon-graham-breaks-team-record-189th-game/ | access-date=2024-09-07}}</ref>

Since the football field had no lights, parents had to shine their car lights on the field for late practices.<ref name=HCah/>  At Crockett, Graham, who had been playing competitive football since age seven,<ref name=TFP/> was expected to make an immediate impact upon joining the football team's starting lineup as a sophomore,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://docs.newsbank.com/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info:sid/iw.newsbank.com:NewsBank:DTNB&rft_val_format=info:ofi/fmt:kev:mtx:ctx&rft_dat=0FD3EB5B03638222&svc_dat=InfoWeb:aggregated5&req_dat=0D0CB579A3BDA420|title=Detroit Public School League|access-date=October 2, 2009|date=August 25, 2003|work=[[The Detroit News]]|author=Markowski, Tom|page=04C}}</ref> and at the end of the season he was recognized as an honorable mention lineman 2003 All-Detroit selection by ''[[The Detroit News]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://docs.newsbank.com/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info:sid/iw.newsbank.com:NewsBank:DTNB&rft_val_format=info:ofi/fmt:kev:mtx:ctx&rft_dat=0FF1DA43250559B8&svc_dat=InfoWeb:aggregated5&req_dat=0D0CB579A3BDA420|title=2003 All-Detroit football team|access-date=October 2, 2009|date=November 26, 2003|work=[[The Detroit News]]|author=Markowski, Tom|page=05C}}</ref>
