{{Short description|American former football player (born 1990)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=April 2014}} {{Use American English|date=December 2024}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Brandon Kaufman | image = | image_size = | alt = | caption = | number = | position = [[Wide receiver]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1990|10|26}} | birth_place = [[Denver, Colorado]], U.S. | death_date = | death_place = | high_school = [[Heritage High School (Littleton, Colorado)|Heritage]] ([[Littleton, Colorado]]) | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 5 | weight_lbs = 235 | college = [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|Eastern Washington]] | draftyear = | draftround = | draftpick = | undraftedyear = 2013 | pastteams = * [[Buffalo Bills]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}–{{NFL Year|2014}})* * [[BC Lions]] ({{CFL Year|2014}})* | highlights = * [[NCAA Division I Football Championship|FCS national champion]] (2010) * College Football Performance Awards FCS Wide Receiver Award (2012) * 2012 FCS Second-team All-American ([[Associated Press|AP]], [[The Sports Network (wire service)|TSN]]) * 2× First-team All-[[Big Sky Conference]] (2012, 2010) * NCAA Division I [[Football Championship Subdivision|FCS]] single-season receiving yards record (2012) }} '''Brandon Kaufman''' (born October 26, 1990) is an American former [[gridiron football|football]] player. He also played [[Australian rules football]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2012-13/Bios/Brandon%20Kaufman |title=Official Eastern Washington Eagles Brandon Kaufman bio |publisher=Goeags.com |access-date=March 14, 2013}} Kaufman played [[college football]] for three years with the [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|Eastern Washington Eagles]]. In 2010, as a sophomore he had 15 [[touchdown]]s, the second-most in school history, to help lead the school to the 2010 NCAA Division I [[Football Championship Subdivision]] National Championship. In 2012, he set the FCS single-season receiving yards record, recording 93 receptions for 1,850 yards and 16 touchdowns. He was a two-time Football Championship Subdivision All-American. He declared early for the [[2013 NFL draft]].{{Cite news |url=http://www.thenewstribune.com/2013/02/23/2486011/wilson-rebuilding-draft-stock.html |title=Wilson rebuilding draft stock | Seattle Seahawks |last=Williams |first=Eric D. |access-date=March 15, 2013 |publisher=The News Tribune |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004221356/http://www.thenewstribune.com/2013/02/23/2486011/wilson-rebuilding-draft-stock.html |archive-date=October 4, 2013 |url-status=dead }} He signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] as a free agent on April 29, 2013. ==Early life and prep career== Kaufman is Jewish, the son of Steve and Rhonda Kaufman.{{cite journal|title=JSR's 2012 College Football All-America Team|journal=[[Jewish Sports Review]]|date=March–April 2013|volume=8|issue=96|page=2}} He was born in [[Denver]], Colorado.{{cite web|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2012/sep/21/ewu-receiver-kaufman-quickly-catches-up/ |title=EWU receiver Kaufman quickly catches up |publisher=Spokesman.com |date=September 21, 2012 |access-date=March 15, 2013}} Kaufman attended [[Heritage High School (Littleton, Colorado)|Heritage High School]] in [[Littleton, Colorado]], graduating in 2009. He competed in track, running [[100 meters]] in 10.8 seconds. He also played basketball for the school, averaging over 13 points a game in 2007.{{cite web |url=http://hscolorado.scout.com/2/820641.html |title=Recruiting Update: Brandon Kaufman |publisher=Hscolorado.scout.com |date=December 12, 2008 |access-date=October 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004214322/http://hscolorado.scout.com/2/820641.html |archive-date=October 4, 2013 |url-status=dead }} He made a highlight reel play his senior season, running away from the basket while falling out of bounds, shooting it one handed from approximately 35 feet and making the three point basket. Playing football for the high school, he was one of the top receivers in Colorado, as he caught 97 passes for 1,918 yards (averaging 20 yards a catch) and 16 touchdowns as a sophomore and junior. Kaufman earned honorable mention All-State honors in football as a junior and twice was selected to the All-Continental League team. He missed his senior season with a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] knee injury suffered during a summer camp before the 2008 season began. Throughout high school, Brandon was known to make highlight reel catches on a regular basis. In practice, he was known to only use one hand during wide receiver drills.{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/combine/profiles/brandon-kaufman?id=2540191 |title=NFL Events: Combine Player Profiles – Brandon Kaufman |work=Nfl.com |access-date=March 15, 2013}} ==College career== ===2009–10=== Because he had been injured in his senior year of high school, all schools other than Eastern Washington University withdrew their offers.{{cite news|url=http://boxscorenews.com/qa-with-ewu-football-player-brandon-kaufman-p10255-68.htm |title=Q&A with EWU Football Player Brandon Kaufman |publisher=Boxscorenews.com |date=July 15, 2009 |access-date=February 27, 2016}} Kaufman played as a true freshman in 2009 for [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|the Eastern Washington Eagles]], a [[Football Championship Subdivision]] school (formerly Division I-AA), seeing action in nine games, including five as a starter. Kaufman finished the year with 23 catches for 294 yards and 1 touchdown. Kaufman was also named to the [[Big Sky Conference]] All-Academic Team. Kaufman helped lead Eastern Washington to the 2010 NCAA Division I FCS National Championship as a sophomore, recording 76 catches (5th-most in school history) for 1,214 yards (also fifth-best in EWU history) and 15 touchdowns (second-best in school history) as he started all 15 games.{{cite web|url=http://www.krem.com/sports/Kaufman-makes-progress-at-EWU-Pro-Day-195807161.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130311140105/http://www.krem.com/sports/Kaufman-makes-progress-at-EWU-Pro-Day-195807161.html |archive-date=March 11, 2013 |title=Kaufman makes progress at EWU Pro Day Spokane |publisher=Krem.com |date=March 6, 2013 |access-date=February 27, 2016}} Kaufman capped off his break-out season with 9 catches for 120 yards in the Championship game against Delaware. With under two minutes left in the 3rd quarter, and with Eastern Washington down 19–0, he caught the first of his two touchdowns helping to spark a rally culminating with his game-winning second touchdown. The final score was 20–19, earning Eastern Washington its first football National Championship. {{cite web|url=http://goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2010-11/releases/11fbJan7DelawareRecap |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919195608/http://www.goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2010-11/releases/11fbJan7DelawareRecap |archive-date=September 19, 2015|title=EAGLES RALLY TO WIN NATIONAL TITLE!!! – Eastern Washington University Athletics |publisher=Goeags.com |date=January 7, 2011 |access-date=February 27, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://m.spokesman.com/galleries/2011/jan/08/ewu-vs-delaware/ |title=EWU vs. Delaware |publisher=M.spokesman.com |date=January 8, 2011 |access-date=October 2, 2013}} Kaufman was named to the First-team All-Big Sky Conference, and named to the ''College Sporting News'' “Sweet 63” All-America Team and the Phil Steele Publications All-America fourth team, and for the second season to the Big Sky Conference All-Academic team. He was also chosen as the NCAA Championship Subdivision Playoffs MVP by ''College Sporting News''. Academically, as of December 2010 he had a 3.57 cumulative [[grade point average]]. ===2011=== Before the 2011 season began, he was named to the 28-member ''[[Athlon Sports|Athlon]]'' College Football Preview preseason All-America team, a pre-season First-team All-American by [[Phil Steele]]’s FCS College Football Preview, one of the top 10 wide receivers in FCS by [[The Sports Network]], one of the top 38 receivers by the College Football Performance Awards, All-Big Sky Conference, and first-team All-BSC by Phil Steele.{{cite web|url=http://www.goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2012-13/Bios/Brandon%20Kaufman |title=Eastern Washington University Athletics: Brandon Kaufman |publisher=Goeags.com |access-date=March 15, 2013}} However, four games into the season he broke a [[metacarpal]] in his left hand against [[Montana State Bobcats football|Montana State]] in September. Kaufman had caught 29 passes for 373 yards at that point. He then [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed in 2011, as an injury hardship case. ===2012=== Before the 2012 season began, he was named a preseason third-team All-American by The Sports Network and AnyGivenSaturday.com, chosen as ont of the top 10 FCS wide receivers by The Sports Network, chosen as the # 6 FCS wide receiver by Phil Steele’s FCS College Football Preview, named preseason All-Big Sky Conference, and listed by Phil Steele as a second-team preseason All-Big Sky selection. In 2012, Kaufman set the FCS single-season receiving yards record, recording 93 receptions for 1,850 yards and 16 touchdowns while leading the Eagles to a semifinal appearance in the 2012 FCS Playoffs.{{cite web|url=http://www.krem.com/sports/Kaufman-to-enter-NFL-Draft-skip-senior-season-186125101.html |title=Kaufman to enter NFL Draft, skip senior season |publisher=Krem.com |date=January 9, 2013 |access-date=March 14, 2013}} Describing his mentality on the field, Kaufman said:
You have to think you’re better than the other person, and trust what you’re doing all week and all year, studying film and what you’re working on in practice. If you do it right, you’ve beaten your guy already all through the week.{{cite web|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2012/dec/01/blanchette-ewus-kaufman-simply-best-player-field/ |title=Blanchette: EWU's Kaufman simply best player on field |publisher=Spokesman.com |date=December 1, 2012 |access-date=March 15, 2013}}
===Records and awards=== In his college career, he caught 221 passes (3rd in EWU history; 7th in Big Sky history) for 3,731 yards (2nd all-time at EWU, 4th in the Big Sky; 16.9 per catch) and 33 touchdowns (2nd in school history) as he started 37 games.{{cite web|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2013/jan/09/kaufman-padron-leaving-ewu-early/ |title=Kaufman, Padron leaving EWU early |publisher=Spokesman.com |date=January 9, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2013}} He was named to the ''[[Jewish Sports Review]]'' 2012 College Football All-America Team. For his career, he was a two-time Football Championship Subdivision All-American. ==NFL career== {{nfl predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 5 | weight =216 | dash = 4.57 | ten split = 1.59 | shuttle = 4.59 | cone drill = 6.83 | vertical = 35.5 | broad ft = | broad in = | bench = | wonderlic = | arm span = | hand span = | note = All values from Eastern Washington [[Pro Day]]{{cite web |url=http://www.goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2012-13/Releases/13fbMarch6ProDay |title=Kaufman Improves Four Marks at Pro Day – Eastern Washington University Athletics |publisher=Goeags.com |date=March 6, 2013 |access-date=October 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005020131/http://www.goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2012-13/Releases/13fbMarch6ProDay |archive-date=October 5, 2013 |url-status=dead }} }} ===2013 NFL draft=== On January 9, 2013, local TV station [[KREM (TV)|KREM]] announced that Kaufman would forgo his final season of eligibility at Eastern Washington, and declared for the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He was 20 credits short of a degree and continued his studies online.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/archive/1682472 |title=Brandon Kaufman, Eastern Washington, NFL Draft |publisher=CBSSports.com |access-date=February 27, 2016}} At an NFL Scouting Combine in Indianapolis in February 2013, he was tested and underwent multiple physicals.{{cite web|url=http://easterneronline.com/2013/02/27/kaufman-works-out-at-nfl-combine/ |title=Kaufman works out at NFL combine |publisher=Easterner Online |date=February 27, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2013}} At an NFL Scouting Combine in [[Cheney, Washington]], on March 6, 2013, he tested before 18 [[National Football League]] scouts at EWU’s annual Pro Day. He had a 68.0 grade (50–69 grades are for those deemed to be a "Draftable Player"; the next higher grades of 70–84 are for "Eventual Starter"), ranking him 18th among 38 wide receivers. He was the second-tallest (6-foot-5) and seventh-biggest (216 pounds) receiver at the combine and had a [[vertical jump]] of 33 1/2 inches. Rob Rang of The Sports Xchange called him a potential fifth- to sixth-round pick. NFLDraftScout.com projected him being picked in the seventh round.{{cite web |author=Andy Hart |url=http://www.patriots.com/news/article-1/Ask-PFW-Combine-queries/f56e1399-4c68-42c8-82fe-0b614388b452 |title=Ask PFW: Combine queries |publisher=Patriots.com |date=February 19, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130327022642/http://www.patriots.com/news/article-1/Ask-PFW-Combine-queries/f56e1399-4c68-42c8-82fe-0b614388b452 |archive-date=March 27, 2013 |url-status=dead }} John Harris of Yahoo! Sports projected that he might be taken by the New York Giants in the 7th round, saying he "has great size and will catch the football going across the middle".{{cite web|last=Harris |first=John |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nfl--2013-new-york-giants-draft-team-needs-focus-up-front-175541628.html |title=2013 Giants draft team needs: Focus up front as New York searches for winning combination |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=March 2, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2013}} Kaufman went undrafted in the [[2013 NFL draft]] but soon signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] as a free agent on April 29, 2013.{{cite web |url=http://www.buffalobills.com/team/roster/Brandon-Kaufman/695112f7-2907-48db-a23a-9425c4847486 |title=Brandon Kaufman |publisher=Buffalo Bills |access-date=April 4, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427062409/http://www.buffalobills.com/team/roster/brandon-kaufman/695112f7-2907-48db-a23a-9425c4847486/ |archive-date=April 27, 2014 |url-status=dead }} ===2013 NFL season=== Kaufman went a perfect six for six, catching all balls thrown to him in the preseason, including one touchdown. (One catch was called back for offensive line holding). His biggest highlight came on his first official catch, against the Colts in game one. The Colts’ sideline read the play before the snap and called in from the sideline to their cornerback that Kaufman was going to run a double-move go route. Despite the advance warning allowing the defender to be in perfect position, Kaufman was still able to pull down the circus catch and get both feet in-bounds. Kaufman consistently was able to get open throughout the preseason, despite very few throws being made overall in the last game in which he saw the most field-time.{{cite web|url=http://www.krem.com/sports/Tuel-Kaufman-excel-in-first-NFL-preseason-game--219217161.html |title=Tuel, Kaufman excel in first NFL preseason game |publisher=Krem.com |access-date=October 2, 2013}}{{cite web|author=MICHAEL MAROT |url=http://niagara-gazette.com/sports/x389853471/FIRST-TEST-A-SUCCESS |title=First Test A Success |date=August 12, 2013 |publisher=Niagara Gazette |access-date=October 2, 2013}}{{cite web|author=AJ Mast |url=https://news.yahoo.com/photos/buffalo-bills-brandon-kaufman-14-makes-catch-against-photo-071134482.html |title=Buffalo Bills' Brandon Kaufman (14) makes a catch against Indianapolis Colts' Daxton Swanson during the second half of an NFL preseason football game on Sunday, Aug. 11, 2013, in Indianapolis. (AP Photo/AJ Mast) |publisher=News.yahoo.com |date=August 12, 2013 |access-date=October 2, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=330816002 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130817053255/http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=330816002 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 17, 2013 |title=Minnesota Vikings vs. Buffalo Bills – Recap – August 16, 2013 |publisher=ESPN |date=August 16, 2013 |access-date=October 2, 2013}}{{cite web |url=http://blogs.buffalonews.com/press-coverage/2013/08/for-bills-bubble-receivers-preseason-finale-an-unfair-catch.html#more |title=For Bills' bubble receivers, preseason finale an unfair catch |publisher=The Buffalo News |date=August 29, 2013 |access-date=October 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004234540/http://blogs.buffalonews.com/press-coverage/2013/08/for-bills-bubble-receivers-preseason-finale-an-unfair-catch.html#more |archive-date=October 4, 2013 |url-status=dead }} The Bills released Kaufman on August 30, 2013.{{cite news | title=Kaufman Keeping NFL Dreams Alive | first=Peter | last=Sowards | url=http://www.khq.com/story/23343168/kaufman-keeping-nfl-dreams-alive | publisher=[[KHQ-TV]] | date=September 4, 2013 | access-date=October 23, 2013}} The Bills signed Kaufman to their practice squad on December 10, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/transactions |title=NFL Transactions Report |work=Nfl.com |access-date=April 4, 2014}} ==Australian football career== {{see also|List of players who have converted from one football code to another}} Kaufman was recruited and signed by the [[Gold Coast Football Club|Gold Coast Suns]] in 2016 to play for their reserves team in the [[North East Australian Football League]]. Kaufman is one of a few Americans to be recruited for the [[Australian Football League|AFL]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goldcoastfc.com.au/news/2016-04-05/gc-suns-confirm-nfl-signing|title=GC SUNS confirm NFL signing Brandon Kaufman|date=April 5, 2016 }} On April 24, 2016, Kaufman played his first game of Australian Rules Football for the Labrador Tigers reserves. Upon return to the US, he played two seasons with the [[Denver Bulldogs]] of the [[United States Australian Football League]]{{Cite web|title=Brandon Kaufman Player Page|url=https://usafl.com/user/5268/matches|url-status=live|website=USAFL.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191103145235/http://usafl.com:80/user/5268/matches |archive-date=November 3, 2019 }} and was in consideration for the USA Revolution National Team scheduled to compete at the 2020 [[Australian Football International Cup]] before it was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web|title=USA Revolution 2020 International Cup Team Announcement|url=https://www.facebook.com/usaflrevolution/photos/2526060584293665|url-status=live|website=Facebook.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117164713/https://www.facebook.com/usaflrevolution/photos/2526060584293665 |archive-date=November 17, 2021 }} ==See also== *[[List of Jews in sports#American football|List of select Jewish football players]] ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== *[http://www.goeags.com/sports/m-footbl/2012-13/Bios/Brandon%Kaufman Official Eastern Washington Eagles bio]{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} {{2010 Eastern Washington Eagles football navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kaufman, Brandon}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Players of Canadian football from Denver]] [[Category:American football wide receivers]] [[Category:Eastern Washington Eagles football players]] [[Category:Buffalo Bills players]] [[Category:BC Lions players]] [[Category:Jewish American players of American football]] [[Category:Players of American football from Denver]] [[Category:Canadian football wide receivers]] [[Category:21st-century American Jews]] [[Category:Jews from Colorado]]

'''Brandon McGee''' (born December 11, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]] and was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in the fifth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
At [[Plantation High School]] in [[Plantation, Florida]], McGee finished his senior year with 31 tackles, two interceptions, one sack and one forced fumble and also had 300 receiving yards. As a junior, he played quarterback in seven games, threw for 1,100 passing yards with 13 touchdowns while also rushing for 450 yards. He was named first-team All-Broward County by ''[[The Miami Herald]]''.

In track, he placed third in the 100 meters at the 2007 FHSAA 4A District 11 Championships with a time of 10.83 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fl.milesplit.com/athletes/97906-brandon-mcgee/feed#.VAYe4fmSwrk|title = Brandon McGee - Feed}}</ref> As a [[University of Miami]] collegiate, he joined the track team and recorded a career-best time of 10.73 seconds in the [[100 meters]] at the 2011 Georgia Tech Invitational.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/MeetResults.aspx?Meet=86795#21100|title = SiteApp}}</ref> He also competed in the [[60 meters|60-meter dash]] and ran a career-best time of 6.83 seconds in the prelims of the 2011 Rod McCravy Invitational.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/MeetResults.aspx?Meet=117788#21100|title=SiteApp}}</ref>

==College career==
McGee attended the [[University of Miami]], and was a member of the [[Miami Hurricanes football]] team from 2009 to 2012. He started 25 of 44 games during his career, recording 109 tackles, three [[interceptions]] and two [[Quarterback sack|sacks]]. As a senior in 2012, he started all 12 games at defensive back and finished tied for sixth on the team with 54 tackles. He recorded a team-high-tying two interceptions and also notched four tackles-for-loss.

===St. Louis Rams===
McGee was selected in the fifth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]] as the 149th pick by the [[St. Louis Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On October 15, 2015, the [[New York Giants]] signed McGee to their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/DB-Brandon-McGee-Tackle-Xavier-Proctor-added-to-Practice-Squad/393866ca-dfe3-46f3-9338-0d1f83229fd9 |title=DB Brandon McGee, Tackle Xavier Proctor added to Practice Squad |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=October 15, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=December 6, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151207040633/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/DB-Brandon-McGee-Tackle-Xavier-Proctor-added-to-Practice-Squad/393866ca-dfe3-46f3-9338-0d1f83229fd9 |archivedate=December 7, 2015 }}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 18, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-add-CB-Brandon-McGee-to-active-roster-waive-TE-Jerome-Cunningham/539a1ed2-783d-4fd4-9d60-8a11fb306fec |title=Giants add CB Brandon McGee to active roster; waive TE Jerome Cunningham |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=October 18, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=December 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121064241/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-add-CB-Brandon-McGee-to-active-roster-waive-TE-Jerome-Cunningham/539a1ed2-783d-4fd4-9d60-8a11fb306fec |archive-date=November 21, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 31, 2015, the Giants announced they had waived McGee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/giants-sign-morris-from-practice-squad-waive-mcgee |title=Giants Waive CB Brandon McGee, Promote LB James Morris |last=Bouda|first=Nate |date=October 31, 2015 |website=[[Fox News]] |access-date=November 9, 2015}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
McGee was signed to the practice squad of the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on December 30, 2015. He signed a reserve/future contract with the Cowboys on January 4, 2016. He was [[waived/injured]] on June 10, 2016 and reverted to injured reserve. McGee was released on July 13, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McGee Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McGeBr00.htm |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On August 23, 2016, McGee signed with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-waive-CB-Keith-Lewis-and-sign-free-agent-CB-Brandon-McGee/cc1c2ec5-c52f-4b99-b670-642492885a82 |title=Lions waive CB Keith Lewis and sign free agent CB Brandon McGee |work=Detroit Lions |date=August 23, 2016 |accessdate=August 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160824145536/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-waive-CB-Keith-Lewis-and-sign-free-agent-CB-Brandon-McGee/cc1c2ec5-c52f-4b99-b670-642492885a82 |archive-date=August 24, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On August 30, 2016, McGee was waived by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions place WR Corey Fuller and TE Brandon Pettigrew on Reserve/PUP|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-place-WR-Corey-Fuller-and-TE-Brandon-Pettigrew-on-ReservePUP/2bceb18c-6aad-4073-ac70-bb0dc9f8da13|access-date=September 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160902161623/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-place-WR-Corey-Fuller-and-TE-Brandon-Pettigrew-on-ReservePUP/2bceb18c-6aad-4073-ac70-bb0dc9f8da13|archive-date=September 2, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McGee's father was diagnosed with [[throat cancer]] in 2000 and his mother with [[breast cancer]] in 2002. His mother died of the cancer in 2004.<ref>[http://www.miamiherald.com/2012/08/31/2977584/journey-isnt-complete-for-miami.html Journey isn’t complete for Miami Hurricanes’ Brandon McGee]</ref>

'''Brandon Hepburn''' (born December 6, 1989) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for [[Florida A&M University|Florida A&M]] and was selected in the seventh round of the [[2013 NFL draft]] by the [[Detroit Lions]].

==Early life==
Hepburn attended [[North Rockland High School]] in [[Thiells, New York]], where he competing in wrestling and played on the football team.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=https://famuathletics.com/sports/football/roster/brandon-hepburn/1184|title=Brandon Hepburn|publisher=Florida A&M Rattlers Athletics|access-date=June 29, 2023}}</ref> As a junior, he recorded 57 tackles and two sacks as a [[linebacker]] and [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]].<ref name=bio/><ref name="success">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/163877505/?clipping_id=127341217|title=North Rockland's Hepburn is well-rounded success|work=[[The Journal News]]|first=Tony|last=Pinciaro|page=15|date=November 10, 2007|access-date=June 29, 2023|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Hepburn was converted to a [[defensive tackle]] ahead of his senior season and recorded 132 tackles, eight sacks and an interception.<ref name=bio/><ref name=success/> He aided his team to a [[NYSPHSAA]] Class AA West title and earned ''[[Journal News]]'' first-team all-county honors.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/916490682/?clipping_id=127346610|title=North Rockland wraps up AA West title, defeating Suffern|work=[[The Journal News]]|first=Alex|last=Myers|page=20|date=October 13, 2007|access-date=June 29, 2023|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/166438478/?clipping_id=127342553|title=Fall All-County|work=[[The Journal News]]|page=101|date=December 9, 2007|access-date=June 29, 2023|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Hepburn was also member of the [[NAACP]] Youth Council, the National Honor Society, the Science Honor Society and the Key Club, earning the ''Journal News'' Scholar-Athlete award as a senior.<ref name=bio/><ref name=success/>

==College career==
Hepburn played college football at [[Florida A&M Rattlers football|Florida A&M]], recording 163 tackles, 15 tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, 11 pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery in four years. Hepburn [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] in 2008 as a [[tight end]] before later being converted to a linebacker. The following year, he was relegated to special teams duty and had 13 total tackles. In 2010, he played in all 11 games recording 63 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble. In his senior year, he put up 86 tackles (9.5 for loss), 5.5 sacks, 7 passes deflected and a forced fumble and was a first-team All-[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] (MEAC) selection.<ref name="draft">{{cite news|url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2013/04/detroit_lions_draft_biochemist.html|title=Detroit Lions draft biochemist Brandon Hepburn with final 2013 draft pick|first=Justin|last=Rogers|date=April 27, 2013|work=[[MLive.com]]|access-date=June 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/5474|title = MEAC FCS Football 2012 All-Conference Teams}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
Hepburn signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on June 8, 2016. On September 3, 2016, he was released by the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web|title=Three Former Draft Picks Among Cowboys' Cuts; McFadden Moved To NFI|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/03/three-former-draft-picks-among-cowboys-cuts-mcfadden-moved-nfi|last=Helman|first=David|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 3, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222185931/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/03/three-former-draft-picks-among-cowboys-cuts-mcfadden-moved-nfi|archive-date=February 22, 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hepburn was born in [[Nyack, New York]], on December 6, 1989, the son of Gregory Hepburn and Adris Swift.<ref name=bio/> His older sister, Yvana, was an All-[[Big East]] hurdler at [[South Florida Bulls track and field|South Florida]].<ref name=bio/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://gousfbulls.com/sports/track-and-field/roster/yvana-hepburn/3029|title=Yvana Hepburn|publisher=South Florida Bulls Athletics|access-date=June 29, 2023}}</ref>

Hepburn credited ''[[The Magic School Bus]]'' and hands-on science kits with igniting his passion for math and science during his early years.<ref name=success/> At Florida A&M, he majored in [[biochemistry]] and was part of an [[undergraduate research]] team investigating cancer treatments using [[copper]].<ref name="research">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/244524749/?clipping_id=127344771|title=FAMU linebacker puts his passion into research|work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|first=St. Claire|last=Murraine|page=1|date=April 3, 2012|access-date=June 29, 2023|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> As a senior in 2012, Hepburn and his team presented their findings at an [[American Chemical Society]] conference in [[San Diego]].<ref name=research/> He was motivated by his grandmother, who had died from cancer six years earlier.<ref name=research/> Hepburn was also the president of the Rattlers Association of Chemists.<ref name=draft/>

As of 2023, Hepburn lived in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/954755738/?clipping_id=127345741|title=Former FAMU stars, NFL players provide advice to draft hopefuls|work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|first=Gerald|last=Thomas III|page=B2|date=April 28, 2023|access-date=June 29, 2023|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

'''Brandon Magee''' (born October 22, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played for the for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) he played for the [[Boston Red Sox]] organization. He also played [[college football]] and [[college baseball|baseball]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils]]. 

==Early life==
Magee attended [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High School]] in [[Corona, California]], where he was a four-year member of both the varsity baseball and football teams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Magee Profile|url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/team/roster/Brandon-Magee/5b78a8af-404f-4c60-9599-df3020050d57|publisher=Cleveland Browns|accessdate=April 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140421120257/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/team/roster/brandon-magee/5b78a8af-404f-4c60-9599-df3020050d57/|archive-date=April 21, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As a senior, he totaled 86 tackles (26 solo), averaging 7.2 tackles-per-game and led the team with 7.5 sacks. He led Centennial High School in sacks as a junior and as a senior.

During his high school career, Magee totaled 193 tackles (60 solo), 11.0 sacks, 7 quarterback hurries, 3 pass deflections and 2 fumble recoveries. He had 13 career games with seven or more tackles and eight games with more than 10.

He was listed as the No. 18 all-purpose athlete in the West region by [[ESPN]] Scouts, Inc. He was rated as the No. 4 weak side linebacker in the West region and the No. 21 weak side linebacker in the nation by [[scout.com]].  He was rated as the No. 26 outside linebacker in the country, the No. 3 linebacker in the state of California and the state's No. 44 overall player by [[rivals.com]].

Magee was coached by Matt Logan at Centennial High School.<ref name="profile">{{cite web|title=Brandon Magee Profile|url=https://thesundevils.com/news/1970/1/1/208251147.aspx|publisher=Arizona State University|accessdate=April 2, 2020}}</ref> During his high school career, Magee was a part of Centennial’s Varsity Football team as they claimed League Titles four consecutive seasons from 2004-2007, as well as [[CIF Southern Section]] Titles in 2004 and 2007.<ref>{{cite web|title=Centennial High School Football|url=http://www.leaguelineup.com/welcome.asp?sid=126700198&url=centennialhuskyfootball|accessdate=April 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407084222/http://www.leaguelineup.com/welcome.asp?sid=126700198&url=centennialhuskyfootball|archive-date=April 7, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He joined his high school teammate Shelly Lyons as member of ASU's 2008 signing class when they both committed to the Sun Devils in January 2008. He ultimately chose ASU over [[University of Arizona]], Louisville, Nebraska, Tennessee and [[Washington State University]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Karpman|first=Chris|title=Centennial linebackers commit to Sun Devils|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2008/brandon-magee-19432|work=Rivals.com|publisher=Yahoo Sports|accessdate=April 2, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Magee accepted a football scholarship from Arizona State University, where he was a double major in Education and Sociology. He was a four-year letterman at ASU where he played in 44 games over five years.

As a [[weakside linebacker]], he accumulated 231 tackles (157 solo). He totaled 10 sacks for a loss of 85 total yards, and 24.5 tackles for losses with a net loss of 115 yards. He had three career interceptions and returned them a total of 56 yards, including one touchdown. Magee had one forced fumble, two fumble recoveries, and three pass deflections.

Magee continued to be a two-sport standout at ASU, as he also was an outfielder for the Sun Devil baseball team. During his college career, the team won consecutive [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] titles and twice went to the [[College World Series]].<ref name=profile/>

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
Magee was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[2013 NFL draft]] on April 28.<ref>{{cite web | title=Cowboys add 15 undrafted players | work= espn.com | date= April 28, 2013 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4708166/cowboys-add-15-undrafted-players |accessdate=April 28, 2020}}</ref> The Cowboys gave him $70,000 in guaranteed money, more than any 2012 seventh-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Michael David|title=Despite $70,000 guarantee, Cowboys cut Brandon Magee|date=August 31, 2013 |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/08/31/despite-70000-guarantee-cowboys-cut-brandon-magee/|publisher=Pro Football Talk|accessdate=April 3, 2020}}</ref> He compiled 16 tackles in the team’s first three exhibition games. He was cut at the conclusion of training camp on August 31.<ref>{{cite web|last=Archer|first=Todd|title=Dallas Cowboys cut down to 53 players|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4713867/cowboys-cut-down-to-53-players|work=espn.com|date=August 31, 2013 |accessdate=April 3, 2020}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On September 1, 2013, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Browns]] after his release from the Cowboys roster.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hensley|first=Jamison|title=Busy day for Browns ends with 6 additions|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4713867/cowboys-cut-down-to-53-players|work=espn.com|date=August 31, 2013 |accessdate=April 3, 2020}}</ref> He appeared in eight games as a [[special teams]] contributor. He was waived on July 23, 2014.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On July 24, 2014, Magee was claimed off waivers by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He was released on August 30 and signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Bucs sign OL, fill practice squad spots | work= espn.com | date= August 31, 2014 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/tampa-bay-buccaneers/post/_/id/5876/bucs-make-roster-moves-2 |accessdate=April 28, 2020}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 15, before being placed on the [[injured reserve list]] with a torn pectoral muscle on December 8. He was waived on March 25, 2015.<ref>{{cite web | title=Magee to try out for Red Sox | work= espn.com | date= March 25, 2015 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12556270 |accessdate=April 28, 2020}}</ref>

Magee was selected by the [[Boston Red Sox]] in the 23rd round of the [[2012 Major League Baseball draft]] and signed with the team in July 2012. Magee was previously drafted by the [[Tampa Bay Rays]] in the 29th round in 2008 and by the [[Oakland Athletics]] in the 21st round in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Magee Profile|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/register/player.fcgi?id=magee-002bra|publisher=baseballreference.com|accessdate=April 3, 2020}}</ref>

He attended [[spring training]] with the Boston Red Sox in 2012, 2013 and 2014 while also playing in the NFL. Magee is the only two-sport professional NFL and MLB athlete in the 21st. century.<ref>{{cite web|last=Carucci|first=Vic|title=Browns Linebacker Brandon Magee Cleveland's version of Bo Jackson?|url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-Linebacker-Brandon-Magee-Clevelands-version-of-Bo-Jackson/1359cb60-d364-4240-a7c8-eba5dcd03f68|publisher=Cleveland Browns|accessdate=April 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140418203551/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-Linebacker-Brandon-Magee-Clevelands-version-of-Bo-Jackson/1359cb60-d364-4240-a7c8-eba5dcd03f68|archive-date=April 18, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

==Philanthropy==
During high school, Magee volunteered for several years in the Corona, CA community along with his brother Angelo and his best friends as they hosted an array of functions for the teenaged population. After Magee's best friend Dominic Redd was murdered while walking home from school, Magee, his brother Angelo and his friends vowed to do all they could to keep their peers safe and off the streets by hosting events such as an annual Halloween party, talent shows and also assisted with the opening of two community youth centers in Corona entitled Mountain Top.

During his time at ASU, Magee visited more than 30 elementary schools across the [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] valley to talk to kids about overcoming obstacles, the importance of education and maintaining a positive mindset. He has also coordinated health fairs for local elementary school children and their families, as well as visited several hospitals, churches and other youth organizations in the Phoenix area. In addition, Magee has been to Canyon State Academy on several occasions to speak about the benefits of academic success and is an active member on ASU's campus.<ref>{{cite web|title=ASU's Brandon Magee Nominated For College Football's Preeminent Community Service Honor|url=https://thesundevils.com/news/2012/7/17/207829208.aspx|publisher=ASU Athletics|accessdate=April 3, 2020}}</ref>

'''Brandon Tyler McManus''' (born July 25, 1991) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Placekicker|kicker]]. He was a member of the [[Denver Broncos]] and their [[Super Bowl 50]] championship team. He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple Owls football|Temple Owls]] and was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in [[2013 NFL season|2013]]. McManus has also been a member of the [[New York Giants]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Washington Commanders]], and [[Green Bay Packers]].

==College career==
McManus holds the [[Temple Owls football|Temple]] career records for points scored (338), field goals made (60), field goals attempted (83), and punting average (45.3).<ref>{{Cite web |last=McLane |first=Jeff |date=February 5, 2016 |title=Temple's McManus living Super Bowl dream |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/20160206_Temple_s_McManus_living_Super_Bowl_dream.html |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=Inquirer.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=Connor |date=July 23, 2014 |title=Brandon McManus Ready for Giants Kicker Competition |url=http://www.bigblueinteractive.com/2014/07/22/brandon-mcmanus-ready-giants-kicker-competition/ |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=Big Blue Interactive}}</ref> As a senior in 2012, he earned All-Big East first-team honors after leading the team in scoring (74) on 14-of-17 field goals and 32-of-33 extra points. He averaged 45.1 yards per punt, pinned 17 punts inside the 20-yard line and had a long kick of 68 yards. McManus handled kickoff duties as well and recorded 40 touchbacks on 56 total kickoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus, K, Temple |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/1725103/brandon-mcmanus |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
After going undrafted in the [[2013 NFL draft]], McManus signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on April 28, 2013. On August 25, McManus was waived prior to the start of the season by Indianapolis.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brandon McManus Contract Breakdowns, Salary Cap Figures, Salaries, Bonuses|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/brandon-mcmanus-12797/transactions/|access-date=May 25, 2023|website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On January 2, 2014, McManus signed a reserve/futures contract with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01.htm |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He played in 4 preseason games for the team prior to being traded to Denver.

===Denver Broncos===
On August 26, 2014, the Giants traded McManus to the [[Denver Broncos]] to cover for the loss of the Broncos' starting kicker [[Matt Prater]], who began the [[2014 NFL season]] serving a four-game suspension. McManus became their starting kicker following the release of Prater on October 3, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=October 3, 2014 |title=Broncos release Matt Prater before suspension ends |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/broncos-release-matt-prater-after-suspension-ends |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> McManus was waived by the Broncos on November 11, 2014, after the team decided to sign free agent [[Connor Barth]] as his replacement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klis |first=Mike |date=November 25, 2014 |title=Broncos waive kicker Brandon McManus, agree to terms with Connor Barth |url=http://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_27010637/kicker-connor-barth-agrees-terms-broncos |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=Denver Post}}</ref> McManus cleared waivers, and was quickly re-signed by the Broncos, spending the rest of the season as the team's kickoff specialist.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2014 |title=Broncos re-sign PK Brandon McManus to practice squad |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/broncos-re-sign-pk-brandon-mcmanus-to-practice-squad |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> In 11 games with the Broncos as the primary placekicker, McManus converted all 41 extra point attempts, as well as nine of 13 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

[[File:Brandon McManus.JPG|thumb|upright|McManus with the Denver Broncos in 2014]]
Going into the 2015 season, the Broncos brought both Barth and McManus to training camp. McManus won the job, proving more consistent than he had been in 2014, and the Broncos cut Barth.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2015 |title=Broncos cut Connor Barth, Brandon McManus wins job |url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2015/08/27/Denver-Broncos-cut-PK-Connor-Barth-Brandon-McManus-wins-job/9141440648594/ |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=UPI}}</ref>  On September 13, 2015, he became the third kicker in NFL history to make multiple field goals of 56 or more yards in the same game, joining [[Sebastian Janikowski]] and [[Greg Zuerlein]], who both achieved the feat in the 2012 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Wolfe |first1=Cameron |last2=Jhabvala |first2=Nicki |name-list-style=amp |date=September 13, 2015 |title=Broncos' bests/worsts vs. Ravens: Brandon McManus and C.J. October 18, McManus made the game winning overtime field goal to propel the Broncos to a 26–23 overtime win over the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 18, 2015 |title=Manning shakes In the 2018 season, McManus converted all 35 extra point attempts and 20 of 25 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the 2019 season, McManus converted 25 of 26 extra point attempts and 29 of 34 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

McManus was named the AFC Special Teams of the Week for his performance in Week 6.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=October 21, 2020 |title=Titans RB Derrick Henry, Falcons QB Matt Ryan lead Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/titans-derrick-henry-falcons-matt-ryan-players-of-the-week |access-date=October 24, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on December 14, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=December 14, 2020 |title=Broncos place K Brandon McManus on Reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-place-k-brandon-mcmanus-on-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> and re-activated on December 23.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=December 23, 2020 |title=Broncos activate K Brandon McManus from Reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-k-brandon-mcmanus-from-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> In the 2020 NFL season, McManus converted 24 of 27 extra point attempts and 28 of 34 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

=== Green Bay Packers ===
On October 16, 2024, McManus was signed by the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 16, 2024 |title=Packers sign K Brandon Mcmanus, release K Brayden Narveson |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-k-brandon-mcmanus-release-k-brayden-narveson-2024 |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> On October 20, 2024, in his first game with the Packers, he kicked a 45 yard game-winning field goal to help Green Bay defeat the Houston Texans 24–22.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demovsky |first=Rob |date=October 20, 2024 |title=McManus wins game for Packers days after signing |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41911600/packers-brandon-mcmanus-kicks-game-winning-field-goal-vs-texans-days-signing |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> McManus kicked a 24 yard game-winning field goal to help Green Bay defeat his former team, the Jacksonville Jaguars 30–27 in his second game with the Packers on October 27.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Jacksonville Jaguars – October 27th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410270jax.htm |access-date=November 4, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In 11 games with the Packers, he converted all 30 extra point attempts and 20-of-21 field goal attempts in the 2024 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 13, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 4, 2025, McManus agreed to a three-year, $15.3 million contract with the Packers, including a $5 million signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demovsky |first=Rob |date=March 4, 2025 |title=Packers bring back kicker McManus on 3-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/44110451/packers-bringing-back-kicker-brandon-mcmanus-3-year-deal |access-date=March 4, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2025 season, he converted 32 of 33 extra point attempts and 24 of 30 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon McManus 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMaBr01/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=March 10, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

During the Packers' [[2025–26 NFL playoffs#NFC: Chicago Bears 31, Green Bay Packers 27|first round]] playoff game against the [[Chicago Bears]], McManus missed a field goal in the second quarter, an extra point attempt in the fourth quarter which would have given the Packers a two-possession lead, and a field goal with less than 3 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter which would have tied the game; the Packers would go on to lose the game 31–27.<ref>{{citeweb |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/robreischel/2026/01/10/the-good-bad-and-ugly-from-the-green-bay-packers-epic-collapse-against-the-chicago-bears/ |title=The Good, Bad And Ugly From The Green Bay Packers’ Epic Collapse Against The Chicago Bears |author=Rob Reischel |website=Forbes.com |date=January 10, 2026 |access-date=January 10, 2026}}</ref>

On May 8, 2026, McManus was released by the Packers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers release K Brandon McManus|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-release-k-brandon-mcmanus-may-8-2026|website=packers.com|date=May 8, 2026|access-date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

==Sexual assault lawsuit==
On May 24, 2024, two flight attendants sued McManus, alleging that he had sexually assaulted them during a team chartered flight from Jacksonville to London in 2023, as the Jaguars were traveling to play consecutive games in London.<ref name="r928">{{cite web | last=Alexander | first=Harriet | title=Jaguars player accused of groping attendants on flight to UK NFL game | website=[[The Times]] & The Sunday Times | date=May 28, 2024 | url=https://www.thetimes.com/world/us-world/article/brandon-mcmanus-super-bowl-winner-groped-attendants-claim-rspkb77jb?region=global | access-date=October 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=McManus accused of sexual assault on Jags flight |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/brandon-mcmanus-accused-of-sexual-assault-on-jaguars-2023-london-flight |publisher=NBC |date=May 28, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Ana Faguy">{{cite news |last1=Faguy |first1=Ana |title=NFL player accused of sexual assault on London flight |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6pp5p4z7jyo |work=BBC News |publisher=BBC |date=May 28, 2024}}</ref> McManus denied the allegations.<ref name="Ana Faguy" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sullivan |first1=Tyler |title=Brandon McManus sexual assault allegations: Ex-Jaguars kicker and the team being sued by two women, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/brandon-mcmanus-sexual-assault-allegations-ex-jaguars-kicker-and-the-team-being-sued-by-two-women-per-report/ |work=CBS Sports |publisher=CBS |date=May 28, 2024}}</ref> The lawsuit also alleged that the Jaguars committed gross negligence by failing to properly train McManus about inappropriate and sexual contact with flight staff, supervise him on the flight, adopt policies and procedures to protect flight staff from sexual misconduct by employees, or enforce a zero-tolerance policy regarding inappropriate behavior.<ref name="f904">{{cite web | last=DiRocco | first=Michael | title=NFL kicker McManus accused of sexual assault | website=ESPN.com | date=May 27, 2024 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/40229099/nfl-kicker-brandon-mcmanus-accused-sexual-assault-lawsuit | access-date=October 3, 2024}}</ref> 

In September 2024, the NFL concluded its investigation into the incident, saying there was insufficient evidence to support a finding that McManus had violated the league's personal conduct policy.<ref name="a187">{{cite web | last=DiRocco | first=Michael | title=NFL: Insufficient evidence to discipline McManus | website=ESPN.com | date=September 30, 2024 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41535426/nfl-discipline-kicker-brandon-mcmanus-source-says | access-date=October 16, 2024}}</ref> That same month, a judge dismissed the women's initial lawsuit, saying their case did not rise to the "exceptional" criteria required for anonymity. The women then filed an amended complaint, this time using their names.<ref>{{cite news |title=Women file amended complaint against NFL kicker Brandon McManus alleging sexual assault |url=https://apnews.com/article/brandon-mcmanus-jaguars-lawsuit-1ef0ec8a47b42b3f0fc76a4e82553274 |access-date=October 16, 2024 |work=AP News |date=September 6, 2024}}</ref> In October 2024, upon being signed by Green Bay, attorneys for both McManus and the accusers stated that the case was "resolved" without providing additional information.<ref name="j882">{{cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=October 17, 2024 |title=Lawsuit against Brandon McManus is "resolved" |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/lawsuit-against-brandon-mcmanus-is-resolved |access-date=October 24, 2024 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

'''Brandon King''' (born June 8, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] and [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). 1,390 of his 1,392 career snaps were on [[special teams]]. He was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2015 and won [[Super Bowl LI]] and [[Super Bowl LIII]] with the Patriots. He played [[college football]] for the [[Highland Scotties]] and [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].

==College career==
Brandon King played at the [[linebacker]] position at [[Thompson High School]] in Alabama and for the [[Highland Scotties]] of the [[Kansas Jayhawk Community College Conference]]. In his sophomore season, King recorded 118 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and was ranked as the fifth best [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the national community college rankings.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://highlandcc.edu/pages/whats-new/highland-alum-signs-with-patriots|title=Highland Alum Signs with Patriots|publisher=Highland Community College|date=2015|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref>

In July 2012, King verbally committed to transfer to the [[University of South Alabama]] and to play for the [[South Alabama Jaguars football|Jaguars football team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2012/07/brandon_king_latest_to_give_ve.html|title=Brandon King latest to give verbal commitment to South Alabama|publisher=Alabama Media Group|date=July 28, 2012|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref> However, in January 2013, King announced that he had changed his mind, and on [[National Signing Day]] a month later, signed to play for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Tigers]] of [[Auburn University]] beginning in the [[2013 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2013 FBS season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.al.com/auburnfootball/index.ssf/2013/01/juco_safety_brandon_king_commi.html|title=JUCO safety Brandon King commits to Auburn|publisher=Alabama Media Group|date=January 4, 2013|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref>

At Auburn, King played behind [[Robenson Therezie]] at the "star" safety position, seeing action in every game of his first season for the Tigers, albeit mostly on [[special teams]]. Halfway through his senior season, King was moved to defensive end by his coaches, who were looking for increased speed at the position.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.al.com/auburnfootball/index.ssf/2014/10/looking_for_speed_auburn_moves.html|title=Looking for speed, Auburn moves Brandon King to defensive end|publisher=Alabama Media Group|date=October 19, 2014|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
King was not ranked as a top safety prospect and did not receive an invitation to the [[NFL Combine]]. On March 3, 2015, King participated at Auburn's [[pro day]], along with [[Cameron Artis-Payne]], [[Angelo Blackson]], [[Quan Bray]], [[Sammie Coates]],  [[Reese Dismukes]], [[Corey Grant (running back)|Corey Grant]], [[Nick Marshall]], [[C. J. Uzomah]], [[Jermaine Whitehead]], [[Gabe Wright]], [[Trovon Reed]], and nine other teammates. ===New England Patriots===
====2015====
On May 8, 2015, the [[New England Patriots]] signed King as an undrafted free agent after he went unselected in the [[2015 NFL draft]]. The contract King agreed to was for three years and $1.57 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.csnne.com/new-england-patriots/patriots-sign-seven-undrafted-free-agents|title=Patriots sign seven undrafted free agents|publisher=Comcast SportsNet New England|date=May 8, 2015|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref><ref name="spotrac"/>

With the Patriots depth at both safety positions, King was relegated to competing for a role on special teams. On September 5, 2015, King was released by the Patriots as part of their final roster cuts and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots release 11 players; Place Brandon LaFell on PUP|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2015/09/05/patriots-release-11-players-place-brandon-lafell-pup|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170608214355/http://www.patriots.com/news/2015/09/05/patriots-release-11-players-place-brandon-lafell-pup|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 8, 2017|website=Patriots.com|date=September 5, 2015|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots sign 10 players to the practice squad|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2015/09/07/patriots-sign-10-players-practice-squad|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171203153843/http://www.patriots.com/news/2015/09/07/patriots-sign-10-players-practice-squad|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 3, 2017|website=Patriots.com|date=September 7, 2015|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> On October 10, 2015, the Patriots signed King to their active roster after releasing cornerback [[Bradley Fletcher]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2015/10/10/patriots-release-db-bradley-fletcher-sign-db-brandon-king-practice-squad|title=Patriots release DB Bradley Fletcher; Sign DB Brandon King from the practice squad|website=Patriots.com|date=October 10, 2015|access-date=October 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151012080713/http://www.patriots.com/news/2015/10/10/patriots-release-db-bradley-fletcher-sign-db-brandon-king-practice-squad|archive-date=October 12, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following day, he made his professional regular season debut and recorded two solo tackles in a 30–6 victory at the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. On November 23, 2015, King collected two solo tackles and forced the first fumble of his career in a 20–13 victory over the [[Buffalo Bills]]. During the third quarter, King was assigned to be the gunner on the punt recovery team, opposite [[Matthew Slater]]. He forced the Bills' punt returner [[Leodis McKelvin]] to fumble and it was recovered by Patriots' linebacker [[Jonathan Freeny]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Patriots rookie Brandon King a 'mismatch guy' on special teams| url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-england-patriots/article/patriots-rookie-brandon-king-a-mismatch-guy-on-special-teams-41357741/| access-date=December 2, 2017| website=247sports.com| author=Oliver Thomas| date=November 24, 2015}}</ref> King finished his rookie season with 12 combined tackles (ten solo) in 13 games and played solely on special teams.<ref name="stats">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon King-2015| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandonking/2553665/gamelogs?season=2015| access-date=December 2, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref> His 12 special teams tackles finished second on the team behind only [[Matthew Slater]]'s 17.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=MikeReiss|author=Mike Reiss|number=685168153970741248|date=January 7, 2016|title=Patriots special teams leading tacklers in 2015: Matthew Slater (17), Brandon King (12), Nate Ebner (11). Next player on the list has 3.}}</ref>

The Patriots finished the season atop the [[AFC East]] with a 12–4 record. On January 16, 2016, King played in his first career playoff game and assisted on a tackle during the Patriots' 27–20 victory In the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] divisional game against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. The following game, he recorded two solo tackles in the Patriots 20–18 loss to the eventual [[Super Bowl 50]] Champions the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref name="stats"/>

====2016–2020====
On April 7, 2016, King signed his exclusive rights free agent tender to remain with the Patriots. The contract terms were for one year and $525,000<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots re-sign RB LeGarrette Blount; Sign exclusive rights free agents DB Justin Coleman and S Brandon King|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2016/04/12/patriots-re-sign-rb-legarrette-blount-sign-exclusive-rights-free-agents-db-justin|website=Patriots.com|date=April 12, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref><ref name="spotrac"/> King competed with [[Cedric Thompson]] throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]] for a job as a backup strong safety. He was named the third string strong safety behind [[Patrick Chung]] and [[Jordan Richards (American football)|Jordan Richards]] to start the season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: New England Patriots' depth chart: 08/01/2017| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/186/NE| access-date=December 2, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On October 16, 2016, King recorded a season-high two combined tackles during a 35–17 victory over the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He finished the 2016 season with ten combined tackles (7 solo) in 16 games and zero starts. On February 5, 2017, King was part of the Patriots team that won [[Super Bowl LI]]. In the game, the Patriots defeated the [[Atlanta Falcons]] by a score of 34–28 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201702050atl.htm|title=Super Bowl LI – New England Patriots vs. Atlanta Falcons – February 5th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=September 2, 2017}}</ref> Throughout the playoffs, he appeared in all three games and assisted on one tackle in the AFC divisional round 34–16 victory over the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon King-2016| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandonking/2553665/gamelogs?season=2016| access-date=December 2, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On April 12, 2017, King signed his exclusive rights free agent tender to remain with the Patriots.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web|title=Brandon King contract details|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-england-patriots/brandon-king-17375/| access-date=December 2, 2017| website=spotrac.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots re-sign exclusive rights free agent DB Brandon King|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/04/12/patriots-re-sign-exclusive-rights-free-agent-db-brandon-king|website=Patriots.com|date=April 12, 2017}}</ref> He made the Patriots' 53-man roster after establishing himself as a core special teamer in his previous two years with the team. On October 29, 2017, King forced his first career safety while defending a [[punt return]] when he tackled [[Travis Benjamin]] in the endzone during the Patriots' 21–13 victory over the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710290nwe.htm |title=Los Angeles Chargers at New England Patriots – October 29th, 2017 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=November 7, 2017}}</ref> The Patriots reached [[Super Bowl LII]], but lost 41–33 to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] with King recording 1 tackle.<ref name="247sports.com">{{cite web | last=Quinn | first=Sam | title=Brandon King offers advice to NFL Combine participants | website=247Sports | date=2019-02-13 | url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-england-patriots/Article/Brandon-King-offers-advice-to-NFL-draft-prospects-129076488/ | access-date=2025-01-19}}</ref>

On March 8, 2018, King signed a two-year contract extension with the Patriots for $2.6 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roundup: Patriots' Brandon King signs two-year deal|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/roundup-patriots-brandon-king-signs-two-year-deal-0ap3000000920179|website=NFL.com|date=March 8, 2018}}</ref> King helped the Patriots reach [[Super Bowl LIII]], which they ended up winning against the [[Los Angeles Rams]] by a score of 13–3 on February 3, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shpigel |first=Ben |date=2019-02-04 |title=Patriots Win in Lowest-Scoring Super Bowl Ever |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/03/sports/patriots-super-bowl.html |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

On May 17, 2019, King signed a two-year contract extension with the Patriots through the 2021 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots sign LB Brandon King to a 2-year extension|url=https://www.patspulpit.com/2019/5/17/18629435/patriots-sign-lb-brandon-king-to-a-2-year-extension|work=Pats Pulpit|date=May 17, 2019}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on August 25, 2019 with a torn quad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Patriots' Brandon King: Placed on IR |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/patriots-brandon-king-placed-on-ir/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=August 25, 2019 |access-date=August 27, 2019}}</ref>

King was placed on the active/[[physically unable to perform list]] (PUP) at the start of training camp on August 2, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=DeArdo, Bryan |title=Patriots place running back Sony Michel, receiver Mohamed Sanu on PUP list, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/patriots-place-running-back-sony-michel-receiver-mohamed-sanu-on-pup-list-per-report/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=August 4, 2020 |access-date=August 4, 2020}}</ref> He was moved to the reserve/PUP list on August 11.<ref>{{cite news |title=Patriots Sign DL Darius Kilgo; Place LB Brandon King on Reserve/PUP List |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-dl-darius-kilgo-place-lb-brandon-king-on-reserve-pup-list |website=Patriots.com |date=August 11, 2020 |access-date=August 13, 2020 |archive-date=August 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200822205043/https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-dl-darius-kilgo-place-lb-brandon-king-on-reserve-pup-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On April 13, 2022, the [[Indianapolis Colts]] signed King.<ref>{{cite web |title=Colts Sign Linebacker Brandon King |url=https://www.colts.com/news/free-agency-sign-brandon-king-patriots-special-teams-linebacker |website=Colts.com |access-date=13 April 2022}}</ref> He was released on August 30, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Final 2022 Roster Cuts|url=https://www.colts.com/news/final-2022-roster-cuts-philip-lindsay-tyson-williams-jack-coan|website=Colts.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

'''Brandon Jennings''' (born July 15, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played his [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]]. Jennings was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in 2000. He played four seasons for the Raiders, [[2002 Cleveland Browns|Cleveland Browns]], [[2002 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]], and [[2003 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]].

Jennings went undrafted in the [[2000 NFL draft]], but was signed by the Oakland Raiders. During his rookie season in 2000 he recorded one tackle.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL #39 Brandon Jennings -ESPN |url=http://espn.com/nfl/playerstats?playerId=2460 |accessdate=September 6, 2018 |website=ESPN.com }}{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On October 14, 2001, Jennings was waived by the Oakland Raiders.<ref>{{cite web |title=Transactions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/10/14/sports/transactions-670391.html |accessdate=September 6, 2018 |website=nytimes.com}}</ref> On October 17, 2001, Jennings was claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Transactions: October 17, 2001 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/2001/10/17/transactions/7c9f3260-8db5-48a8-994a-3583578f0d0d/ |accessdate=September 6, 2018 |website=washingtonpost.com}}</ref> On October 24, 2001, Jennings was waived by the Cleveland Browns. On October 29, 2001, the Oakland Raiders signed Jennings to their [[practice squad]]. On November 7, 2001, the Oakland Raiders promoted Jennings to their active roster. On November 14, 2001, the Oakland Raiders released Jennings from their active roster and re-signed him to their practice squad two days later. Jennings recorded 12 combined tackles in [[2001 NFL season|2001]] and appeared in eight games.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Jennings (2001) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandonjennings/2504073/gamelogs?season=2001 |accessdate=September 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On September 1, 2002, the Oakland Raiders released Jennings as part of their final roster cuts. On October 9, 2002, the [[Green Bay Packers]] signed Jennings to their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wednesday's Sports Transactions |url=https://www.myplainview.com/news/article/Wednesday-s-Sports-Transactions-8996153.php |accessdate=September 6, 2018 |website=myplainview.com |date=October 9, 2002}}</ref> On October 15, 2002, the Green Bay Packers released Jennings from their practice squad. On October 24, 2002, the Oakland Raiders signed Jennings to their practice squad. The following day, the Oakland Raiders promoted Jennings from their practice squad to their active roster. On January 12, 2003, the Oakland Raiders waived Jennings. On January 27, 2003, the [[Houston Texans]] claimed Jennings off of waivers. On February 27, 2003, the Houston Texans offered Jennings a one-year, [[United States dollar|$]]605,000 tender as a [[restricted free agent]]. One March 21, 2003, it was reported that Jennings had officially signed his restricted free agent tender with the Houston Texans. On  August 13, 2003, the Houston Texans released Jennings as part of their roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Jennings news, rumors, and stats |url=http://www.kffl.com/player/7756/nfl/brandon-jennings |website=kffl.com |access-date=2018-09-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906195832/http://www.kffl.com/player/7756/nfl/brandon-jennings |archive-date=2018-09-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Brandon Knight''' (born April 1, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2019. He played [[college football]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]].

==Early life==
Knight attended [[Noblesville High School]] in [[Noblesville, Indiana]]. He was a two-time All-conference selection. As a senior, he received Associated Press Class 6A All-state honors. He originally committed to [[Purdue University]] to play college football, but changed his commitment to [[Indiana University]].

==College career==
As a freshman, he appeared in 11 games, playing as an [[offensive tackle]] or [[tight end]]. He had his lone reception, a 22-yard touchdown, in the 54–36 win against [[Purdue University]], which sealed a bowl berth. He was named honorable-mention BTN.com All-Freshman.<ref name="article">{{Cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2018/08/09/iu-football-brandon-knight-indiana-hoosiers/924542002/ |title=Healthy 'hometown kid' Brandon Knight will be key for IU football offensive line |last=VanTryon |first=Matthew |date=August 9, 2018 |website=Indiana Star |access-date=February 18, 2020}}</ref>

As a sophomore, he appeared in the first 8 games, starting six at [[right tackle]] after fifth-year senior Dimitric Camiel had back surgery. He suffered a season-ending left leg injury against the [[University of Maryland]].<ref name=article/>

As a junior, an unspecified injury kept him out of the early season games, but was able to return to play in the final 10 contests with 8 starts at [[right tackle]].<ref name=article/>

As a senior, he started all 12 games at [[right tackle]], allowing three sacks in 904 snaps. He received honorable-mention All-Big Ten honors at the end of the season. He finished with 41 career and 26 starts at [[right tackle]].

===Dallas Cowboys===
Knight signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2019 NFL draft]] on May 10.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Knight Has Guard/Tackle Flexibility|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/brandon-knight-has-guard-tackle-flexibility|website=dallascowboys.com|accessdate=August 18, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in 7 games in 2019, with one start. He started at [[right tackle]] against the [[New York Jets]], as an injury replacement for [[La'el Collins]].

In 2020, reserve swing tackle [[Cameron Fleming]] was not re-signed, opening the door for Knight to become the backup at [[left tackle]]. After starter [[Tyron Smith]] was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] due to a neck surgery, the Cowboys announced that Knight would fill in as the replacement. He underwent a knee scope after Week 6 and was placed on injured reserve on October 24, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys move starting LT to IR, again, open Door No. 3|url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/24/dallas-cowboys-roster-moves-ir-brandon-knight-cam-erving/|work=Cowboys Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=October 24, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on November 21, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Henry, Asa |title=Cowboys activate OT Brandon Knight, add Tyler Biadasz to IR |url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/21/dallas-cowboys-week-11-roster-moves-brandon-knight-tyler-biadasz-rashard-robinson-adam-redmond/ |website=USAToday.com |date=November 21, 2020 |accessdate=December 27, 2020}}</ref> He appeared in 13 games with 9 starts at [[left tackle]].

In 2021, he was mostly a reserve [[offensive tackle]], playing only 3 snaps in one game. On October 16, 2021, Knight was waived by the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys roster moves: Two signed from practice squad, one waived, Tyron Smith expected to play|url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2021/10/16/22730059/dallas-cowboys-roster-moves-two-signed-from-practice-squad-one-waived-tyron-smith-expected-to-play|work=Blogging the Boys|publisher=SB Nation|date=October 16, 2021}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On October 18, 2021, Knight was claimed off waivers by the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Awarded Offensive Tackle Brandon Knight Off Waivers|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-awarded-offensive-tackle-brandon-knight-off-waivers|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 22, 2021}}</ref> He was acquired to provide depth on the [[offensive line]] while [[Ronnie Stanley]] recovered from an ankle injury. On October 21, 2021, Knight announced that he elected not to join the team, in order to focus on his mental health. The Ravens placed him on the reserve/did not report list to keep his player rights.<ref>{{cite web|title=OT Brandon Knight does not report to Ravens, will 'take a break from football' to focus on mental health, family|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32448062/ot-brandon-knight-does-not-report-ravens-take-break-football-focus-mental-health-family|author=Hensley, Jamison|website=ESPN|date=October 21, 2021|access-date=October 22, 2021}}</ref>
