He finished the season with a total of 79 combined tackles (48 solo), five sacks, two pass deflections, and one interception in 15 games and 13 starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Brandon Jones stats (2021)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneBr06.htm |access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 53.4 from Pro Football Focus.<ref>{{cite web| title=Updated NFL roster rankings for all 32 teams for 2022: Strengths, weaknesses and X factors for every starting lineup| url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-roster-rankings-all-32-teams-2022-strengths-weaknesses-x-factors-every-starting-lineup| access-date=April 15, 2025| website=PFF.com| date=September 4, 2022| author=Ben Linsey}}</ref>

====2022====
{{see also|2022 Miami Dolphins season}}
On January 10, 2022, the Miami Dolphins officially fired head coach [[Brian Flores]] after a 9–8 record in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins fire head coach Brian Flores after three seasons |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dolphins-fire-head-coach-brian-flores-after-three-seasons| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=NFL.com |date=January 10, 2022}}</ref> On February 6, 2022, the [[2022 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] announced their decision to hire [[2021 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers']] offensive coordinator [[Mike McDaniel]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins hire Mike McDaniel as new head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dolphins-working-toward-deal-to-hire-mike-mcdaniel-as-new-head-coach| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=NFL.com |date=February 6, 2022| author=Grant Gordon}}</ref> Defensive coordinator Josh Boyer returned as defensive coordinator under McDaniel and Jones and Jevon Holland remained as the starting safety duo to start the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Any surprises as Miami Dolphins release first depth chart of regular season?|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/2022/09/06/miami-dolphins-release-first-depth-chart-2022-season/7995992001/| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=palmbeachpost.com |date=September 6, 2022| author=Hal Habib}}</ref>

On September 11, 2022, Jones started in the Miami Dolphins' home opener and recorded a season-high 11 combined tackles (six solo), deflected a pass, and had one sack in a 20–7 victory against the [[2022 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New England Patriots at Miami Dolphins - September 11th, 2002|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209110mia.htm| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> On October 25, 2022, the Miami Dolphins officially placed Jones on [[injured reserve]] after suffering a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in Week 7.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2022/10/25/dolphins-brandon-jones-calvin-jackson/|title=Dolphins place Brandon Jones on IR, sign WR to the practice squad|website=DolphinsWire.com|publisher=USAToday.com|date=October 25, 2022|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> He finished the [[2022 NFL season]] with 49 combined tackles (26 solo), three pass deflections, and two sacks in seven games and seven starts at free safety.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pro-Football-Reference: Brandon Jones stats (2022)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneBr06.htm| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref>

====2023====
{{see also|2023 Miami Dolphins season}}
On January 19, 2023, the [[2023 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] fired defensive coordinator [[Josh Boyer]]. Throughout training camp, Jones competed against close friend and former college teammate [[DeShon Elliott]] for the starting role at free safety. New defensive coordinator [[Vic Fangio]] named Jones the primary backup safety, behind starters DeShon Elliott and [[Jevon Holland]] to begin 2023.<ref>{{cite web| title=They're close friends reunited with the Dolphins. But they can't agree on one thing| url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nfl/miami-dolphins/article278081007.html| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=MiamiHerald.com |author=Meadow Barrow| date=August 18, 2022}}</ref>

Jones was inactive for the Dolphins' Week 9 loss at the [[2023 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] due to a [[concussion]]. He started four consecutive games (Weeks 13–16) at safety after Jevon Holland was sidelined due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web| title=Holland One Step Closer to Returning| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/dolphins/news/jevon-holland-working-his-way-back-in-dolphins-defense| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=si.com |author=Omar Kelly| date=December 27, 2023}}</ref> On December 17, 2023, Jones made five solo tackles and had a career-high two interceptions off of [[Trevor Siemian]] as the Dolphins routed the [[2023 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] 0–30.<ref>{{cite web| title=New York Jets at Miami Dolphins - December 17th, 2023| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202312170mia.htm| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He finished with 48 combined tackles (36 solo), four pass deflections, two interceptions, and a forced fumble in 16 games and five starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Brandon Jones stats (2023)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneBr06.htm| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 75.4 from Pro Football Focus, which ranked 17th among all qualifying safeties in 2023.<ref>{{cite web| title=Highest-graded safeties from the 2023 NFL season: Antoine Winfield Jr. shines| url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-highest-graded-safeties-2023-nfl-season| access-date=April 15, 2025| website=PFF.com| date=March 1, 2024| author=Lauren Gray}}</ref>

The [[2023 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] finished the [[2023 NFL season]] second in the [[AFC East]] with an 11–6 record to clinch a Wild Card spot. On January 13, 2024, Jones started in his first career playoff appearance and recorded eight combined tackles (four solo) in a 7–26 loss at the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC Wildcard Game.<ref>{{cite web| title=Wild Card - Miami Dolphins at Kansas City Chiefs - January 13th, 2024| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401130kan.htm| access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
====2024====
{{see also|2024 Denver Broncos season}}
On March 11, 2024, the [[Denver Broncos]] signed Jones to a three–year, [[United States dollar|$]]20 million [[contract]] that includes $11 million guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] of $5.50 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign S Brandon Jones to 3-year contract|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-s-brandon-jones-to-3-year-contract|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=March 14, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Spotrac"/>

Throughout training camp, Jones competed against former [[2019 Texas Longhorns football season|Texas Longhorns]] teammates [[Caden Sterns]] and [[P. J. Locke]], as well as [[JL Skinner]] for a starting role at safety after the departures of former starters [[Justin Simmons (American football)|Justin Simmons]] and [[Kareem Jackson]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Broncos Camp: P.J. Locke, Brandon Jones, Caden Sterns to lead safety room| url=https://milehighsports.com/broncos-camp-preview-p-j-locke-brandon-jones-caden-sterns-to-lead-safety-room/ |access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=milehighsports.com |date=July 10, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Broncos' updated safety depth chart without Caden Sterns| url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2024/08/05/denver-broncos-safety-depth-chart-without-caden-sterns/ |access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=broncoswire.usatoday.com |date=August 5, 2024| author=Jon Heath}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Brandon Jones says it's 'really cool' to reunite with Texas teammates in the NFL| url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2024/07/09/denver-broncos-brandon-jones-texas-teammates-in-the-nfl/ |access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=broncoswire.usatoday.com |date=July 9, 2024| author=Jon Heath}}</ref> Head coach [[Sean Payton]] named Jones and P. J. Locke the starting safety tandem to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Broncos' updated safety depth chart without Caden Sterns| url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2024/09/04/broncos-news-2024-depth-chat-released-bo-nix-starting-quarterback/ |access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=broncoswire.usatoday.com |date=August 5, 2024| author=Jon Heath}}</ref>

On September 22, 2024, Jones made six combined tackles (four solo), a pass deflection, and made his first interception with the Denver Broncos after picking off a pass by [[Baker Mayfield]] intended for [[Mike Evans (wide receiver)|Mike Evans]] and returned it for a career-best 37-yards in a 26–7 win at the [[2024 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Broncos at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - September 27th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202409220tam.htm |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> In Week 6, he racked up a career-high 11 solo tackles (12 combined) and deflected a pass during a 16–23 loss to the [[2024 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]]. He was sidelined for a Week 11 win against the [[2024 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] due to an abdominal injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Injury Report: S Brandon Jones questionable for Week 11 vs. Falcons, three players ruled out|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/injuryreport/injury-report-s-brandon-jones-questionable-for-week-11-vs-falcons-three-players-ruled-out |access-date=January 10, 2025| website=denverbroncos.com|date=November 15, 2024}}</ref> In Week 15, Jones had nine combined tackles (eight solo), a career-high three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Anthony Richardson (American football)|Anthony Richardson]] as the Broncos defeated the [[2024 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] 31–13. On December 28, 2024, he collected a career-high 13 combined tackles (nine solo) in a 24–30 loss at the [[2024 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]. He finished the [[2024 NFL season]] with 115 combined tackles (79 solo), ten pass deflections, three interceptions, one forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pro-Football-Reference: Brandon Jones stats (2024)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneBr06.htm |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 86.7 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which ranked fifth among 171 qualifying safeties in 2024.<ref name="PFF">{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Brandon Jones| url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/brandon-jones/43049| access-date=April 15, 2025| website=PFF.com}}</ref>

==== 2025 ====
On December 15, 2025, Jones was placed on injured reserve after suffering a pectoral injury in a Week 15 win against the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-12-15 |title=Broncos claim RB Cody Schrader off waivers, place S Brandon Jones on IR |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-claim-rb-cody-schrader-off-waivers-place-s-brandon-jones-on-ir |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> He finished the regular season with 78 tackles, seven passes defensed, and one interception through 14 games (13 starts). On January 13, 2026, it was reported that Jones had undergone surgery to repair a torn pectoral muscle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 13, 2026 |title=Broncos' Brandon Jones: Out at least two more games |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/broncos-brandon-jones-out-at-least-two-more-games/ |access-date=January 19, 2026 |website=cbssports.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Brandon Hill''' (born September 6, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]].

==Early life==
Hill grew up in [[Apopka, Florida]] and attended [[Wekiva High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carnahan |first=J.C. |date=2018-08-20 |title=Wekiva football game-changers ready to tackle upcoming season |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2018/08/20/wekiva-football-game-changers-ready-to-tackle-upcoming-season/ |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref> He was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Pittsburgh from 23 total scholarship offers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 30, 2018 |title=Wekiva safety Brandon Hill talks about committing to Pitt |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2018/07/01/wekiva-safety-brandon-hill-talks-about-committing-to-pitt/ |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Hill played in four games during his true freshman season while preserving a redshirt on the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hammett |first=Jim |date=November 3, 2020 |title=Pitt turns to Brandon Hill to replace Paris Ford |url=https://pittsburgh.rivals.com/news/pitt-turns-to-brandon-hill-to-replace-paris-ford?yptr=yahoo%3Fsrc%3Drss |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref> He made 27 tackles with two forced fumbles and one interception as a redshirt freshman.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garrett |first=Tommy |date=April 8, 2023 |title=Brandon Hill, S, Pitt: NFL Draft Scouting Report |url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/brandon-hill-s-pitt-nfl-draft-scouting-report-2023/ |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=ProFootballNetwork.com}}</ref> Hill was named  second team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) as a redshirt sophomore.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Chris |date=December 29, 2021 |title=Former Wekiva stars Tyler Davis, Brandon Hill cherish All-ACC selections |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/os-sp-local-all-conference-tyler-davis-brandon-hill-20211229-fngigqdzcffjrfxfw4jh2orjke-story.html |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref> He had 67 tackles and two passes broken up during his redshirt junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carter |first=Christopher |date=March 3, 2023 |title=Brandon Hill looks to uphold strong Pitt defensive backs reputation at NFL scouting combine |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2023/03/03/nfl-combine-pitt-panthers-brandon-hill-nfl-draft-acc-pat-narduzzi/stories/202303020118 |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=[[Pittsburgh Hill was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] in the seventh round, 248th overall, of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Brandon Hill chosen by Texans, 8th Pitt defensive back drafted in past 6 years |url=https://triblive.com/sports/brandon-hill-chosen-by-texans-8th-pitt-defensive-back-drafted-in-past-6-years/ |access-date=April 30, 2023 |website=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]}}</ref> He was waived on August 29, 2023, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Texans announce initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-announce-initial-53-man-roster |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (8-30-2023) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-8-30-2023 |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> Hill signed a reserve/future contract with Houston on January 22, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 22, 2024 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-22-2024) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-22-2024 |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

On August 25, 2024, it was announced that Hill would miss the entirety of the 2024 season after suffering a right knee injury in the team's preseason finale.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sources: Texans safety Brandon Hill out for season with significant knee injury|url=https://www.click2houston.com/sports/2024/08/24/texans-defensive-backs-brandon-hill-kris-boyd-carted-off-in-rams-preseason-game-case-keenum-heads-to-locker-room/|access-date=August 30, 2024|website=click2houston.com|language=en}}</ref> 

The Texans waived Hill on March 17, 2025, after a failed physical.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2025 |title=The Houston Texans made a roster move |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-17-2025 |access-date=March 17, 2025 |website=HoustonTexans.com |language=en}}</ref> He was re-signed to the team's practice squad on December 16.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (12-16-2025)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-12-16-2025|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=December 16, 2025}}</ref> Hill was released by the Texans on December 23.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (12-23-2025)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-12-23-2025|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=December 23, 2025}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On December 30, 2025, Hill was signed to the [[Las Vegas Raiders]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite tweet|title=We have signed S Brandon Hill to the practice squad.|user=Raiders|number=2006111823762739644}}</ref>

===Houston Texans (second stint)===
On January 14, 2026, Hill was re-signed to the Houston Texans practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-14-2026)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-14-2026|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=January 14, 2026}}</ref>

'''Brandon Kemp''' (born January 18, 1997) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[offensive lineman]] for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Valdosta State Blazers football|Valdosta State]].

==Early life==
Kemp played [[high school football]] at [[Columbia High School (Georgia)|Columbia High School]] in [[Decatur, Georgia]].<ref name="ajc">{{cite web | url=https://www.ajc.com/lifestyles/the-midst-pandemic-nfl-dream-put-hold/ht1kSukfE6KIMaPg5wESHL/ | title=In the midst of a pandemic, an NFL dream is put on hold | publisher=ajc.com | date=May 7, 2020 | accessdate=February 29, 2024 | author=Staples, Gracie Bonds}}</ref>

==College career==
Kemp played [[college football]] at [[Valdosta State Blazers football|Valdosta State]] from 2016 to 2019.<ref name="dbstats">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/brandon-kemp-kempbr01 | title=Brandon Kemp | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref> He was [[redshirted]] in 2015.<ref name="bio">{{cite web | url=https://vstateblazers.com/sports/football/roster/brandon-kemp/3622 | title=Brandon Kemp | publisher=vstateblazers.com | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref> He started 11 games in 2016, earning first team All-[[Gulf South Conference]] (GSC) honors.<ref name="dbstats"/><ref name="bio"/> Kemp appeared in seven games, starting five, in 2017. He played in 12 games, starting 11, in 2018, garnering second team All-GSC recognition and helping Valdosta State win the [[NCAA Division II]] national championship.<ref name="bio"/> He appeared in 11 games in 2019, earning first team All-GSC and second team [[Associated Press]] Little [[All-America]] honors.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/dec/19/2019-ap-little-all-america-team-2019121/ | title=2019 AP Little All-America Team | publisher=nwaonline.com | date=December 19, 2019 | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://vstateblazers.com/news/2020/4/25/football-kemp-inks-priority-free-agent-contract-with-tennessee-titans.aspx | title=Kemp Inks Priority Free Agent Contract with Tennessee Titans | publisher=vstateblazers.com | date=April 25, 2020 | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref><ref name="dbstats"/>

==Professional career==

Kemp signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) on May 7, 2020, after going undrafted in the [[2020 NFL draft]]. He was waived on September 5 and signed to the team's [[practice squad]] on September 6, 2020. He was signed to a futures contract on January 11, 2021. Kemp was placed on [[injured reserve]] on July 31, 2021. He was released on April 7, 2022.<ref name="db">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/brandon-kemp-kempbr01/transactions | title=Brandon Kemp | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref>

Kemp was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the NFL on April 15, 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/colts/news/colts-sign-mountainous-offensive-tackle-brandon-kemp | title=Colts Sign Mountainous Offensive Tackle Brandon Kemp | publisher=si.com | date=April 15, 2022 | accessdate=February 29, 2024 | author=Arthur, Jake}}</ref><ref name="db"/> He was released on August 16, 2022.<ref name="db"/>

Kemp signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on September 20, 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.insauga.com/brandon-kemp-joins-hamilton-tiger-cats-after-nfl-stints-with-colts-titans/ | title=Brandon Kemp joins Hamilton Tiger-Cats after NFL stints with Colts, Titans | publisher=insauga.com | date=September 20, 2022 | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref><ref name="dbstats"/> He was placed on injured reserve on September 22, activated from injured reserve on October 28, and placed on injured reserve again on November 5, 2022.<ref name="db"/> Overall, he played in one game, a start, for the Tiger-Cats in 2022.<ref name="dbstats"/> Kemp was moved to the practice roster on June 8, 2023. He was placed on, and activated from, injured reserve several times during the 2023 season.<ref name="db"/> He appeared in 10 games, all starts, for the Tiger-Cats in 2023.<ref name="dbstats"/> Kemp was re-signed by the team on December 14, 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/hamilton-tiger-cats-sign-offensive-214626243.html | title=Hamilton Tiger-Cats re-sign offensive linemen Brandon Kemp, Jakub Szott | publisher=ca.sports.yahoo.com | date=December 15, 2023 | accessdate=February 29, 2024}}</ref><ref name="db"/>

On January 7, 2025, it was announced that Kemp had signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-07 |title=Riders Sign Offensive Lineman Brandon Kemp |url=https://www.riderville.com/2025/01/07/riders-sign-offensive-lineman-brandon-kemp/ |access-date=2025-02-14 |website=Saskatchewan Roughriders |language=en}}</ref> He was part of the final cuts at the end of training camp on June 1, 2025.<ref name=2025T>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2025/ |title=Transactions – Football Player Trades and Signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=August 7, 2025}}</ref>

On July 3, 2025, it was announced that Kemp had signed with the [[Massachusetts Pirates]] of the [[Indoor Football League]] (IFL).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://masspiratesfootball.com/news/2025/7/3/football-pirates-sign-ol-brandon-kemp-presented-by-gulf.aspx|title=Pirates Sign OL Brandon Kemp|website=Massachusetts Pirates|first=Mick|last=Moninghoff|date=July 3, 2025|access-date=August 17, 2025}}</ref>

On August 5, 2025, it was announced that Kemp had signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref name=TORsigned>{{Cite web |url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2025/08/05/argonauts-add-ol-ryan-sceviour-rb-peny-boone-ol-brandon-kemp/ |title=Argonauts Add OL Ryan Sceviour, RB Peny Boone & OL Brandon Kemp |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |date=August 5, 2025}}</ref>
